Copenhagen label led by founder Sigurd Bank, focused on cut, fabric and longevity using deadstock, recycled and organic materials; the SS27 collection 'Deadlines' marked 10 years in business with 'overworked' office-wear-inspired silhouettes.

Copenhagen-based women's label by designer Casey Larkin Blond, rooted in eclectic, individualistic dressing inspired by travel, vintage and real life; the SS27 collection 'Lucky' was the brand's first-ever runway show, marking 13 years since its Copenhagen relaunch.
Fashion and lifestyle brand by Astrid Andersen; 'Stel' means body in Danish, reflecting an inclusive design ethos built around function and longevity.

Nigerian label founded in 2009 by Bubu Ogisi, blending heritage textiles with traditional African craft techniques; winner of the Zalando Visionary Award 2025; the SS27 collection 'Sacred Ecologies' explored cultural displacement through raffia, beads and hand-crafted materials.

Finnish design house founded in 1951, globally renowned for its art of printmaking and bold prints; creative director Rebekka Bay; the SS27 runway show celebrated the art, the artist and the landscape.

Graduate showcase from the Swedish School of Textiles in Borås, Sweden — a standout of over 20 experimental student collections, from embroidered LIDL bags and tops made of hair to LED-light dresses and coats made of tights.

Copenhagen womenswear label by designer Nicklas Skovgaard, founded in 2020, known for narrative-driven collections and innovative fabrication; SS27 dressed 'The Skovgaardettes,' a fictional '60s girl group who emerged from vintage Ford Mustangs in layers of gingham and peplum.

Copenhagen-based clothing label founded in 2022 by Caroline Bille Brahe, rooted in intuition, playfulness and great craftsmanship; expressive, limited-number pieces from the atelier in Borgergade, often using deadstock Chanel, Dries Van Noten and Harris tweed; SS27 'Caro Club' channeled nightlife glamour.

Brazilian label designed by founder and creative director Patricia Bonaldi, in business for about 20 years and in the U.S. for a decade. Known for Brazilian artisan embroidery, fringe, dimensional detailing and draping across beachwear and eveningwear; the collection is manufactured in Brazil. Sold at Saks Fifth Avenue, Bloomingdale’s, Revolve and Bergdorf Goodman. Introduced footwear for fall 2026 and an eyewear collection for spring 2027.
Paris-based label co-founded by designer Danial Aitouganov and stylist Imruh Asha; known for bold color, playful silhouettes and a childlike spirit. 2025 LVMH Prize finalist.
Belgian designer (b. 1965, Liège); launched her eponymous Paris label in 1991 after working as an assistant to Azzedine Alaïa; works from her atelier-showroom at 32 boulevard Ménilmontant, Paris.

One of the most important designers in SPFW history. Since the 1990s, Alexandre Herchcovitch's work has combined technical mastery, alternative-culture references and precise construction, with a rare ability to turn restlessness into clothing; he reclaimed control of his eponymous label via licensing from the InBrands group.

Created by Vivian Rivaben and Silvio de Marchi, Forca Studio works an aesthetic tied to rebellion, São Paulo nightlife and urban subcultures — oversized proportions, high-impact materials and an attitude-loaded image. The brand treats the runway as experience, extending its narrative into set design, casting and performance.

Founded in 1972, the Brazilian jeanswear label helped build the public's relationship with denim as a symbol of youth, attitude and urban life. A subsidiary of the InBrands group, it returns to the SPFW calendar after approximately four years.

The Ceará-based label founded in 2017 by Marina Bitu and Cecília Baima translates Brazilian craft techniques through a contemporary, colorful and experimental language — enlarged fuxicos, pleats, richelieu lace and manually built surfaces — with a strong sustainability value.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Transforms urban, sporty and vintage references into fashion with immediate personality — utilitarian pieces, wide proportions, graphic elements and an eye for reuse — converting street codes into runway imagery. Designer and new-business director Alexandre Herchcovitch leads the brand alongside its ÀLG line.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Latin America's leading e-commerce marketplace participates as a special project rather than a traditional fashion label. In past seasons it worked with stylist Daniel Ueda's curation to build looks from different decades, trends and products available on the marketplace, connecting content, styling, technology and commerce.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Tom Martins made Martins known for a maximalist aesthetic marked by clashing prints, volumes and musical references with an almost performative energy — while also knowing when to strip elements back and work in silence. An unpredictable presence each season.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Designer Mayari Jubini brings haute couture, technology and sculptural design together at Artemisi — 3D printing, crystals, rigid structures and futuristic surfaces in a recognizable visual vocabulary that treats the body as a space of experimentation, readable as garment, object and performance.

Designer, artist and professor, Gustavo Silvestre took crochet into a field of experimentation spanning fashion, art and sustainability. His work connects to Projeto Ponto Firme, an initiative promoting education and social transformation through crochet in the prison system, challenging the old separation between craft and high fashion.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Founded by Celina Hissa of Ceará, the brand built its trajectory on collaboration with artisan women and the valorization of handcraft knowledge — crochet, bobbin lace, carnauba straw and other Ceará techniques — and became a reference in production transparency, centering the women and communities behind each piece.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: A partnership between Sou de Algodão, the movement promoting Brazilian cotton, and Ronaldo Fraga, one of the country's most narrative-driven designers. Fraga turns fashion into memory, research and cultural commentary, and the collaboration bridges the production chain, national identity and the imagination of a creator who treats clothing as storytelling.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Part of a generation raised mixing fashion, music, internet, games and pop culture. His collections move between East and West, fantasy and urban life, with layering, volumes and characters that seem to belong to their own universes; he has dressed artists including Shakira, Anitta and Gloria Groove, turning the runway into a stage for new imaginaries.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: João Pimenta turned menswear tailoring into a territory of freedom — skirts, dresses, light fabrics and volumes in dialogue with suits, shirts and classic codes. His work questions gender limits without abandoning technical rigor, with literature, theater and behavior frequently running through his collections.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Founded in 2006 by sisters Lilly and Renata Sarti, the brand built a feminine image balancing sensuality, precise design and sophisticated materials — leather, architectural cutouts, prints and shape-shifting pieces that work desire without relying on the obvious.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Created by engineer-turned-designer Mônica Sampaio, Santa Resistência celebrates Afro-Brazilian aesthetics and the cultural roots of the Recôncavo Baiano. Prints, fluid dresses, tunics and intense colors appear in a production tied to slow fashion and a more conscious chain, turning ancestry into contemporary presence.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: One of the names that helped project Brazilian beachwear beyond the country. After the trajectory built with Rosa Chá, Amir Slama develops an eponymous label of cutouts, prints, sensuality and attention to the body; his return to the lineup reinforces a creator who understands beachwear as fashion, behavior and Brazilian identity.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: The Minas Gerais label under the creative direction of Giovanna Resende works embroidery, transparencies, velvets, cutouts and references to Minas baroque; the 'Doura' collection showed how ancestral techniques can gain sensuality and contemporary reading. It arrives at SPFW after its first fashion-week collection at RioFW in April.

Founded by André Namitala in Rio de Janeiro, Handred developed a light, solar tailoring connected to the Brazilian way of dressing — breathable fabrics, loose silhouettes and artistic references forming a sophisticated fashion without rigidity, keeping uncomplicated elegance as its signature.

After more than a decade away from the calendar, Marcelo Sommer returned to SPFW with Uó, a project dedicated to upcycling and transforming existing garments. The name plays with what was considered outdated, disposable or bad taste; in the designer's hands, treasure-hunting becomes authorial construction.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Created by Ana Luisa Fernandes in 2018, Aluf developed a language that brings fashion, art, architecture and sensibility together. Textures, volumes and natural materials appear in constructions that follow the body without losing presence; the brand values artisanal process and treats sustainability as part of creation, not just discourse.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Created by stylist Marco Normando and visual artist Emídio Contente, the Amazonian-origin brand uses tailoring, material research and Amazonian references to shift the gaze of Brazilian fashion to the North — working symbols, mythologies and urban contradictions into precisely constructed fashion with territorial identity.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: A special project dedicated to training and accelerating talent from São Paulo's peripheries. The initiative combines technical instruction, creative development and runway experience, expanding entry possibilities into the market — renewing Brazilian fashion also means opening paths for those historically distant from the big calendars.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Founded in Salvador by Hisan Silva and Pedro Batalha, Dendezeiro turned Bahian experiences into an expansive, affective and politically conscious fashion language — colors, volumes, memory, celebration and belonging without reducing Bahia to a tourist image. It returns to SPFW as one of the most vibrant voices of the new Brazilian fashion.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Created by Antônio Castro of Alagoas, Foz connects tailoring, craft and Brazilian popular culture. Its collections value techniques and professionals working outside the market's most obvious centers, especially in Alagoas — embroidery, textures and manual constructions with a contemporary finish that never erases the origin of the knowledge used.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Debuting at SPFW under the creative direction of Amanda Felisberto, Ammi was created in 2018 and bets on handmade pieces and an idea of luxury built through time, technique and a network of artisans — crochet, transparencies and elaborate surfaces forming a feminine, solar and contemporary image.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Founded by Luiz Cláudio Silva, Apartamento 03 emerged in Belo Horizonte and carries in its name the memory of the space where the designer served his first clients. The brand combines technical mastery, tailoring, embroidery and narratives tied to Black identity and the Brazilian experience — precision balanced with emotion.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Contemporary womenswear combining refined luxury, restrained trends, relaxed elegance, and minimal design.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Premium Korean womenswear launched in 2011; original graphics reinterpret nature, light, history, art, and culture through an oriental-fantasy lens.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Duo-founded unisex streetwear label launched in 2017; vivid color, positive storytelling, and borderless styling.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Eponymous house launched in 1985, known for architectural collections blending Korean tradition, calligraphy, and innovative technique.

Seoul-based womenswear founded in 2017 by sisters Sooy and Jay Park; inspired by the 19th-century British Arts and Crafts movement, with a sustainable-luxury approach combining laser-cutting technology and traditional handcraft.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Seoul womenswear label founded in 2013, known for refined tailoring, architectural silhouettes, modern femininity, and technology and couture influences.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Socially and environmentally conscious label associated with upcycling discarded canvases and fabrics, deconstruction, and high-end streetwear.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Founded in 2014; combines menswear-derived structure with feminine softness and reconstructed tailoring.
Korean unisex label; debuted at Seoul Fashion Week in Spring 2025.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Tech-couture label founded in 2022, combining AI, robotics, 3D printing, advanced sustainable materials, and traditional craft.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Founded in 2018; Maison Modern Art Museum translates childlike doodles into wearable art layered over classic, minimalist silhouettes.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Premium womenswear line of DINT focused on modern women, refined elegance, strength, high-sensitivity fabrics, and delicate silhouettes.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Korean high-end menswear house launched in 1987, emphasizing tailoring, structural beauty, craft, bright color, and distinctive detail.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Womenswear label centered on soft, elegant, feminine urban silhouettes with curves, ruffles, trimming, applique, restrained couture detail, and neutral palettes.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Contemporary lifestyle label launched in 2012, known for bold sculptural proportions, tailoring, and Korean cultural references.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: Founded in 2009 after the designer spent 15 years at major Korean fashion houses; known for bold prints, saturated color, unconventional silhouettes, and fashion-tech experimentation.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Unisex contemporary label with genderless formalwear, bold color, and wool and cashmere; Italian-trained tailoring, with the founder having studied at Istituto Marangoni and interned at Moschino.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Young Seoul label known for monochrome gothic styling, leather, biker references, long black coats, and melancholic runway narratives.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Womenswear and streetwear label associated with expressive mix-and-match styling, bold color, oversized silhouettes, clashing prints, and mixed textiles.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Korean menswear label launched in 2005, with a long Seoul Fashion Week history and international showcases.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: Collective design studio launched in 2019, spanning fashion, architecture, photography, graphics, and content; genderless contemporary streetwear.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: Young contemporary womenswear with a modern, playful aesthetic and signature blue.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: Seoul-based menswear label launched in 2004, combining high fashion with a sporty casual aesthetic; known for clean lines, color blocking, and collaborations with Puma, Heineken, Absolut, and MAC.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: South Korean streetwear brand combining American subculture with an urban edge; bold graphics, striking logos, and relaxed silhouettes. The name combines MAHA, Indonesian for greatness, and GRID, representing checkered pattern.

Shanghai-based clothing brand known for a minimalist, zen-inspired aesthetic rooted in oriental elements and humanism. Its stores and Jiading District headquarters (designed by Yiduan Shanghai, Dezeen, 2018) blend natural materials and unfinished surfaces, extending the brand into a lifestyle concept combining garments, tea, incense, homewares and books.

Qingdao-born designer educated in London: BA in womenswear at the London College of Fashion and MA in womenswear knitwear at the Royal College of Art (2013). Known for experimental, sculptural knitwear in bright colors that offers a witty commentary on the fashion system. Launched her label in 2015; shortlisted for the LVMH Prize that same year; shows at London and Shanghai Fashion Weeks with stockists including Dover Street Market, 10 Corso Como and H-Lorenzo (BoF 500).

Hangzhou-born, Shanghai-based designer who graduated with a BA and MA in Fashion from the Royal Academy of Fine Arts, Antwerp, and launched her eponymous brand in 2018. Known for a modern romantic, maximalist aesthetic of striking color, prints, silk jacquards and intricate embroidery, with asymmetry and experimentation in silhouette; shortlisted for the BOF China Prize and the LVMH Prize, and creator of a Hennessy Chinese New Year 2025 collaboration.
Founded in Shanghai in 2015 by Guan Lin, a Parsons and Donghua University graduate; the womenswear label is known for clean lines and a simple, relaxed approach to modern dressing.
Gomeroi label founded by Colleen Tighe-Johnson that translates commissioned Gomeroi artworks and Dreaming stories into one-off garments, alongside a youth-development social enterprise.

Aboriginal luxury swim and resortwear house founded by Larrakia woman Verity van Ermel Scherer as a tribute to her grandmother, Stolen Generations survivor Valerie “Mattie” van Ermel Scherer; known for silk crêpe kaftans and limited-edition swimwear.
Melbourne-based designer; RMIT graduate who worked with Donna Karan in New York and Cerruti in Paris before launching his label in the late 1990s; known for sculptural couture and ready-to-wear.

Australian made and owned luxury ready-to-wear label founded by Co-Founder and Creative Director Gabriella Pereira; launched at AFW 2021; Sydney-designed and locally made in limited runs, championing masterful tailoring and slow fashion.

shows.venue: Park Hyatt Sydney Boardwalk at The Rocks
shows.bio: Australian fashion house founded by Carla Zampatti in 1965; known for power dressing, precision tailoring and eveningwear.
Sydney swim and resortwear label founded in 2017 by Richard Jarman, inspired by seaside living and the idea of a purposeful pause.

shows.venue: Studio One, Legs On The Wall, Sydney
shows.bio: Australian womenswear designer known for fluid draping and precise tailoring.

Contemporary Australian label combining clean lines, languid and sculptural silhouettes, luxury fabrication and a blend of classic and avant-garde influences, spanning unisex ready-to-wear and made-to-order.
Australian fashion house founded in 2008 by Adrian Norris and Edwina Forest, dedicated to raw beauty, tough femininity and effortless cool, bridging coastal and urban dressing.

Sydney-based fashion and textiles designer who launched his eponymous label in 2021; known for emotionally charged garments blurring poetry, digital culture and physical craft, with text-laden prints and sculptural silhouettes; named Emerging Designer of the Year at the 2023 Australian Fashion Laureate.
Contemporary Australian womenswear label founded in 2012.

Label by Sydney designer Hannah Teresa, known for dark romanticism and elevated wardrobe staples; stocked at Reborne Shop, the independent Sydney retail space she also directs. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.
Label by designer Samantha Diorio, known for sensual, modular, seasonless pieces. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.
NIDA-trained designer working between fashion and theatre, known for a corsetry-heavy, performance-inflected presentation. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.
Label by designer Jackie Galleghan, known for quiet restraint and collections honouring craft, storytelling, motherhood and womanhood. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.

Emerging designer exploring the body through innovative material systems, integrating coding and embroidery; known for 3D-printed twin sets shown at the Melbourne Fashion Festival 2026 National Graduate Showcase. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.

Designer whose collection ‘Darlings of the Opera Cassette’ drew on an imaginary opera theatre held within a cassette tape, with surreal corsetry manipulated into otherworldly silhouettes. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.
Slow, consciously created Australian luxury label founded by Charlotte Hicks, built around restraint, quality and longevity, organised as seasonless ‘Editions’.
Byron Bay label founded by Laura May Gibbs with her sister and collaborator Hannah Gibbs, combining art, sustainability and functionality across fashion and activewear.
Australian tailoring and lifestyle label founded by husband-and-wife co-creative directors Joe Farage and Katy Farage.
Label by Dubrovnik-born, Sydney-based designer Karla Špetić, who founded her eponymous line in 2008; known for soft tailoring and a romantic tension between feminine fabrics and sharper silhouettes.
Sydney prêt-à-couture designer known for architectural silhouettes, structured tailoring, fluid drapery and hand embellishment.

shows.venue: Foundation Hall, Museum of Contemporary Art Australia
shows.bio: British-born, Melbourne-based menswear designer; started in men’s footwear before launching a full menswear wardrobe; winner of the 2019 National Designer Award, redefining modern Australian menswear in the space between formal and casual.
Experimental, non-gendered fashion house founded by Jordan Gogos, centred on co-design, upcycling, textile innovation and sculptural wearable art.
Australian luxury womenswear brand established around 2000, known for tactile, natural fabrics and enduring, unconventional design.
Sydney demi-couture label founded in 2014 by Katie-Louise and Lil Nicol-Ford; ethically made to order, working with remnant textiles and queer-history narratives.

Australian concept brand established in 2019, exploring art through pleats and colour; founded by Iuliia Ievdokymenko and Breeana Smith, producing exclusively engineered pleat forms in partnership with one of the world’s oldest pleating factories.

Sydney knitwear designer and UTS Fashion & Textiles graduate who debuted her collection OCEANA — an entirely Shima Seiki-knitted collection inspired by Australia’s marine life — in AFW’s New Gen showcase.
A collaboration between artist Alice Van Meurs and Sarrita King, presented in AFW’s New Gen emerging-designer showcase.

South Sudanese designer behind the label By Gloria Chol; her debut collection ‘Lines of Power’, noted for sculptural silhouettes, dramatic tailoring and elongated denim forms, was featured by Vogue Australia.
First Nations label shown on the Beyond Blak Runway at Melbourne Fashion Festival 2026; selected for AFW’s New Gen emerging-designer showcase.

Contemporary premium un-gendered Australian label founded in 2025; refined minimalism and directional design in small-run production using premium designer deadstock fabrics and local Australian manufacturing; winner of the National Designer Award for Sustainability at Melbourne Fashion Festival 2025.

Sydney-based eponymous label established in 2003; custom made-to-order fine-art collections hand painted by the designer onto ethically sourced eco-cotton, known for masterful drape, intelligent silhouettes and artful colour.

Sustainable First Nations womenswear label founded in 2018 by Wiradjuri entrepreneur Denni Francisco; collaborates with First Nations artists to transpose artworks onto premium-quality garments — Ngali translates to ‘we’ or ‘us’ in several Aboriginal languages.

Sydney-based fashion house by designer Amber Keating, known for streamlined pieces with bold textures — bias-cut dresses, sheer minis and exaggerated blazers — and a rebellious, nonconformist spirit; staged its first runway show in a Potts Point warehouse.

Tokyo-based label launched in 2004 by Yoshio Kubo, who graduated from Philadelphia University's Textile & Science school in 2000, assisted Robert Danes in New York for four years, and returned to Japan in 2004.
Founded in Taiwan in 2017 by Tzu Chin Shen; contemporary womenswear exploring gender, culture, and border-crossing narratives.
Founded in 2025 by Elmo Su; natural materials, quiet beauty, material evolution, and timeless aesthetics.
Established in 2011; Mizuki Ueda launched the label and serves as creative director.
International runway platform committed to curating the future of fashion through diversity and emerging creative voices; the SS27 show featured Nar Rew Ekar, PERRY JONES, and SHINO.
shows.cd: Shoshoni Hostler / Shinobu Uchida / Perry Jones

shows.bio: Partnership presentation by BENCH/ featuring designers Jaggy Glarino, Joey Samson, and Rhett Eala.
shows.cd: Jaggy Glarino / Joey Samson / Rhett Eala

shows.bio: Women's ready-to-wear label established in 1999 by Norio Surikabe, who studied at Kuwasawa Design School and worked in Italy, including at Romeo Gigli and 10 Corso Como's NN Studio.
Established in 2018; Mitsuru Okazaki studied at Ito Garment Research Institute, joined Yohji Design Institute, and worked in pattern production.

Launched in 2016 and rebranded for 2021 A/W as an outerwear-focused label; '360-degree beautiful garments' with functionality, sculptural silhouettes, and an ageless, genderless approach. Meg Miura graduated from ESMOD JAPON and worked under Yoichi Nagasawa.
Established in May 2025 by Eitarou Kamimura, born in Yamaguchi in 2001, recipient of the 97th Soen Award and NEW ENERGY Special Award in June 2023; runway debut September 2025.

Established in 2021; textile-led fashion brand focusing on ways nature has been transformed by human intervention — gardens, botanical gardens, cultivated species — creating imaginary flora and fauna as original textile designs.
Knit brand led by Ryota Murakami, who launched his own brand in 2014; the label changed its name from RYOTAMURAKAMI to pillings in the 2021SS season.

Tokyo label established in 2019, handcrafted in its Tokyo atelier; Yusho Kobayashi graduated from Central Saint Martins after Ritsumeikan University, Tamami Uehara studied textile design at Tama Art University.
Organized by the Taiwan Textile Federation, TAIWAN SELECT is a joint runway presentation showcasing selected Taiwanese fashion brands during Rakuten Fashion Week Tokyo.

Established in 2016 by Tetsuya Doi; unisex label known for constructive forms and dynamic design. Doi graduated from Bunka Fashion Graduate University and studied at coconogacco under Mikio Sakabe and Yoshikazu Yamagata.

Established in 2022, advocating 'Slow Fashion, Slow Luxury' and centering Japanese artisans and craft; Shunsuke Teranishi studied architecture at Kyoto University and worked at Yohji Yamamoto, Carol Christian Poell, Agnona, and Hermès before co-founding MIZEN.
Established in 1955; hat house spanning Akio Hirata OHKO, H.at, and saki et show.
shows.cd: Ohko Hirata / Saki Hirata / Show Hirata

shows.bio: Established in 2019; Taiwan-based brand researching how craft, gestures, and cultural memory remain in materials, including Taiwanese lacquer and Kyoto wax-resist dyeing. SS27 theme 'Becoming,' presented as 'THE ATELIER IS OPEN' — its first-ever Tokyo presentation.
Founded in Taiwan in 1985 by designer Cha-Rin Yeh; the label draws on Taiwanese culture, nature, and lived memory in sharp, gender-neutral urban chic.

Established in 2020 by Sonia Martínez; tailoring, craftsmanship, and construction, revealing hidden garment-making processes. Martínez studied at IED Madrid and worked at Zara, Alexander McQueen, and Phoebe Philo's Céline.

Self-taught French designer based in Paris, born December 1993; known for sculptural hoods, pop-culture, cinema, and video-game references, and signature overlock construction; won the 2026 ANDAM Pierre Bergé Prize.
Established in 2012; Thai craftsmanship, textile experimentation, and geometric silhouettes by designer Wisharawish Akarasantisook.

Established/relaunched in 2025 by Anna Choi; combines Japanese craftsmanship, New York sensibility, European couture techniques, and Korean heritage. Choi previously founded HAENGNAE and works between Tokyo and New York.
Established in 2012 around the concept 'Clothes that will transform you into a HERO for somebody'; opened the flagship store REBLICHAL in Suidobashi in 2017.
Men's and women's ready-to-wear, shoes, bags, and accessories label.

Founded in Tokyo in 2019 by an anonymous design collective; draws on flea-market discovery, folk art, humor, memory, and nostalgia; Tokyo Fashion Award 2023 recipient and LVMH Prize 2024 semifinalist. The SS27 show was presented through Rakuten's 'by R' support project.

Launched in 2018 by Tsukasa Kudo; prioritizes comfort, silhouettes, and clothing grounded in everyday life. Kudo studied at the Royal Academy of Fine Arts Antwerp and worked at Jacquemus, JW Anderson, and Y/Project.

shows.bio: Contemporary menswear label known for handloom fabrics and richly textural work, combining refined craftsmanship with modern silhouettes.

shows.bio: Modern Indian menswear label founded by Central Saint Martins-trained Sahil Aneja, combining refined craftsmanship, tailoring, and contemporary silhouettes.

shows.bio: Chennai-based label founded by NIFT Chennai graduate Vivek Karunakaran, known for clean, minimal, structured silhouettes and form.

shows.bio: Mumbai label founded in 2015 by Sohaya Misra, offering accessible everyday luxury in adjustable, free-size silhouettes crafted from organic cotton, linen, recycled cotton, and post-consumer fabrics.

shows.venue: Fountain of Joy, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 1992 by David Abraham and Rakesh Thakore, a contemporary, non-conforming label rooted in Indian craft, material, form, and urban identity.

shows.bio: New Delhi-based menswear label founded by Kartik Kumra, blending Indian artisan techniques — hand-spun, embroidered, naturally dyed fabrics — with streetwear; winner of the Fashion Trust Arabia 2025 Guest Country Award.
Anamika Khanna’s age- and gender-agnostic label bridging the luxurious and the relaxed, with intricate Indian nuances and silhouettes that transcend geographies.

shows.debut: GenNext debut at Lakmé Fashion Week x FDCI
shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2018 in Delhi by Pearl Academy graduate Jubinav Chadha, known for fantasy- and mythology-inspired couture and pret across menswear and womenswear, translating travel and folklore into engineered textiles.

shows.debut: GenNext debut at Lakmé Fashion Week x FDCI
shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Mumbai-based menswear label founded by Taarini Anand, known for expressive craft-driven menswear inspired by Indian art and miniature painting, handloom khadi, hand-knitting and crochet.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Launched in 2023 in Mumbai by Saim Ghani, a NIFT Kolkata graduate and former senior designer at Anamika Khanna, known for draped silhouettes and sculptural detailing rooted in Indian costume and indigenous street styles.

shows.venue: Atelier, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Student showcase by NIF Global (the New York Institute of Fashion) at Lakmé Fashion Week x FDCI, presenting collections by emerging designers from its centres across India.

shows.venue: Atelier, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Launched in 2010 in New Delhi by Payal Pratap, a NIFT graduate who previously assisted Rajesh Pratap Singh, known for contemporary craft-based womenswear built on Indian textiles, texture, patchwork and intricate embroidery.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2005 by Bihar-born designer Samant Chauhan, known for championing Bhagalpuri handwoven silks, cottons and natural fabrics with intricate hand embroidery in contemporary silhouettes.

shows.bio: An initiative of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) and the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) repositioning khadi through design, innovation, branding and storytelling.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Launched in 1999 in New Delhi by menswear designer Pawan Sachdeva, known for sharp tailoring, precise fit and minimal refined essentials across occasion wear and menswear staples.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Launched in 2009 in Nagpur by Shruti Sancheti (as Pinnacle by Shruti Sancheti), known for contemporary ready-to-wear rooted in Indian textiles, weaves and embroidery, with an emphasis on wearability, comfort, femininity and timeless silhouettes.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2024 by Varshne B in Chennai, a circular menswear label built on indigenous textiles, khadi, naturally dyed Weganool, deadstock fabrics, and waste leather offcuts; winner of the R|Elan Circular Design Challenge 2025.

shows.venue: Atelier, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2008 by Rahul Mishra in New Delhi, known for handmade couture built on Indian handlooms, traditional craft, and intricate embroidery.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in October 2020 by Deepit Chugh in Mumbai, known for menswear blending clean tailored looks with sporty minimalism in an experimental yet wearable approach.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2017 by husband-and-wife duo Neelanjan Ghosh and Kanika Sachdev, known for travel-inspired storytelling, statement prints, and collections rooted in Indian textile crafts like Chanderi, cutwork, and embroidery.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Jaipur-based label founded by Prasoon Sharma, known for bold, colour-saturated streetwear and menswear with handcrafted detailing and retro-bohemian references.

shows.venue: Atelier, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2018 by Aisha Rao in Hyderabad, known for upcycled luxury occasion wear with vibrant appliqué motifs made from fabric waste, overlaid with aari, zardozi, and macramé.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2012 by Bhumika Sharma in New Delhi, known for feminine, elegant occasion wear with vivid floral prints and rich handcrafted embroidery including dabka, tila, and sequins.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2010 by Ritika Mirchandani in Mumbai, known for modern Indian occasion wear inspired by art history, with geometric cutwork, bugle-bead embroidery, belted jackets, and pre-pleated saris.

shows.venue: Atelier, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2011 in Mumbai by Anjali Patel Mehta, a conscious luxury resort and travel-wear label known for story-based hand-illustrated prints, Indian artisanal techniques, fine embroidery, and sustainable fabrics.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2012 by Amit Aggarwal, the eponymous label is known for sculptural couture and luxury prêt shaped through experimental materials such as polymers and liquid organza, combining futuristic structure with Indian handcraft.

shows.venue: Atelier, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Designer Anurag Gupta, winner of the eleventh NEXA ‘The Spotlight,’ uses experimental textile engineering and architectural construction to connect natural forms with technology.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: ‘First Cut’ is the student showcase presented by Pearl Academy, India’s leading creative-education institution established in 1993, in collaboration with the FDCI, presenting the debut collections of final-year fashion students.

shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Launched in the UAE in 2004 by Landmark Group and introduced to India in 2006, a value-fashion retail brand known for affordable, trend-led clothing, footwear, and accessories for women, men, and children.

shows.debut: Aditi Rao Hydari’s debut as co-creative director
shows.venue: Runway, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 1985 by Satya Paul, the heritage Indian label is synonymous with bold, graphic prints — polka dots, zebra stripes, abstract graphics, and art-inspired motifs — and contemporary reinterpretations of the sari.

shows.debut: péro’s first-ever grand finale showcase
shows.venue: Atelier, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2009 in New Delhi by Aneeth Arora, a textile-led label known for relaxed, generous silhouettes and richly handmade fabrics combining Indian weaving, embroidery, crochet, appliqué, and patchwork with a contemporary global sensibility.

Founded in 2020 by Emi Funayama, the Tokyo womenswear label is known for body-conscious silhouettes — sheer fabrics, lace and cut-out techniques — built around the concept “The Figure: Feminine.” Funayama won the first JFW Next Brand Award.
Founded in 2019 by designer Lee Hye Yeon; carefully constructed garments balancing bold design with basics, emphasizing sincerity, longevity, and resistance to fleeting trends.
Label by designers Park Youn Young and Lee Woo Sung; studies structure, proportion, and material under the theme ‘Until Minimalism Becomes Audacity.’
shows.cd: Park Youn Young & Lee Woo Sung

shows.bio: Ready-to-wear label by designers Byungmun Seo and Jina Um — menswear since 2012, womenswear since 2015; rebellious sophistication through deconstruction and reinterpretation of classic luxury.
Seoul-based contemporary label; quiet, considered everyday design across outerwear, knitwear, dresses, and accessories, with clean construction and wearability.

Founded in 2021 by designer Sungmin ‘Jaden’ Cho; studied fashion design at Kookmin University and completed an MA in Womenswear at the Royal College of Art; reinterprets Korean clothing’s structure, ornamentation, functionality, and craftsmanship.
Founded in 2019 by designer and traditional-costume researcher Yeji Kim; the name joins ‘riu’ (flow) and ‘viu’ (view), reinterpreting traditional Korean dress for contemporary life.

Meta Campania Collective is a Paris-based menswear label founded by creative director Jon Strassburg, inspired by the nonchalant "artist's uniform" of figures like Pablo Picasso and Wolfgang Tillmans; every piece is made in Italy.

Études Studio is a Paris-based multi-disciplinary collective founded in 2012 by Aurélien Arbet and Jérémie Egry, expressing itself through contemporary menswear, art direction and independent art-book publishing.
Founded in Tokyo in 2014 by Hiroaki Sueyasu; the menswear label draws from punk and street culture.
Founded in 1961 by Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé; credited with bringing the tuxedo (Le Smoking) into womenswear. Anthony Vaccarello has been creative director since 2016.

Valette Studio is a Paris-based tailoring label founded in 2020 by Pierre-François Valette, an Institut Français de la Mode graduate who trained at Isabel Marant and Saint Laurent; the house designs and produces locally in Paris under the Fabriqué à Paris label.
Founded in Tokyo in 2015 by Ryota Iwai; the label is known for luxurious Japanese fabrics and minimalist design.
Founded in 1854 by Louis Vuitton as a Parisian trunk maker, long before it became a ready-to-wear house. Nicolas Ghesquière has led womenswear since 2013; Pharrell Williams leads menswear.
Founded in 1970 by Japanese designer Kenzo Takada; Nigo became artistic director in 2021. Part of LVMH.

shows.venue: Fondation Simone et Cino Del Duca
shows.bio: Founded in Paris in 1895 by Alessandro Berluti as a bespoke shoemaker; the LVMH-owned maison is known for Venezia leather patina and luxury menswear.

Founded in 1946 by Christian Dior; the 1947 “New Look” reshaped postwar fashion and still anchors the house's silhouette today. Jonathan Anderson became sole creative director in 2025, the first person to oversee womenswear, menswear, and couture together.

3.Paradis is a French-Canadian menswear label founded in 2013 by Emeric Tchatchoua, fusing tailoring and streetwear with graphic storytelling rooted in his Parisian, Cameroonian and Montreal influences.

shows.venue: Hôtel de La Marck (Belgian ambassador's residence)
shows.bio: Belgian designer who launched her eponymous label in 2020 after stints at Marc Jacobs and as head of Dries Van Noten womenswear; winner of the 2025 ANDAM Grand Prix.

Founded in 1996 in Stockholm by Jonny Johansson, part of a wider ACNE (“Ambition to Create Novel Expression”) creative collective spanning photography, art, and design. Johansson remains creative director.
The menswear line of Solid Homme, founded in Seoul in 1988; known for minimalist Korean menswear.
Founded in Paris in 1991 by Christophe Lemaire; the label, designed with Sarah-Linh Tran, is known for understated, functional elegance.
Founded in Paris in 1993 by Zio Song; the menswear house blends Eastern philosophy with Parisian tailoring.
Bluemarble is a Paris-based menswear label founded in 2019 by Anthony Alvarez, blending surf and skate influences with early-2000s nostalgia and a multicultural perspective.
Jeanne Friot is a Paris-based genderless brand founded in 2020 by its namesake designer, producing limited-edition pieces from recycled and upcycled materials, made in France.
Egonlab. is a Paris-based fashion label founded in 2019 by Florentin Glémarec and Kévin Nompeix, known for sharp, experimental tailoring that bridges generations through romance and rebellion.

shows.venue: Former Fondation Cartier building, Boulevard Raspail
shows.bio: Founded in Paris in 2011 by Alexandre Mattiussi; the menswear label offers relaxed Parisian chic with the Ami de Cœur logo.

Founded in 1952 by Hubert de Givenchy, closely associated with Audrey Hepburn's screen wardrobe in the 1950s and '60s. Sarah Burton has been creative director since 2024, following two decades at Alexander McQueen.

Song for the Mute is an Australian menswear label founded in 2010 by Melvin Tanaya and Lyna Ty, developing each collection as a narrative "chapter" in oversized silhouettes crafted from artisanal Italian and Japanese fabrics.

shows.venue: Reflecting pool at Palais de Tokyo
shows.bio: Founded in Los Angeles in 1994 by Rick Owens, the label is known for gothic, grunge-inflected architectural silhouettes. Owens' dark, monumental aesthetic has made him one of fashion's most distinctive independent voices.

The Miyake Design Studio was founded in Tokyo in 1970 by Issey Miyake, built on textile experimentation, pleating and technology. Satoshi Kondo has directed the ISSEY MIYAKE collection since Spring/Summer 2020.
shows.cd: Sen Kawahara, Yuki Itakura, and Nobutaka Kobayashi

shows.bio: Ouest Paris is a menswear label founded by Arthur Robert, fusing Parisian sensibilities with the spirit of the American West through raw denim, surf and skate codes, and workwear.
Beijing-based menswear designer; the label is known for refined tailoring with Chinese cultural references.
Founded in London in 2015 by Feng Chen Wang; the menswear label blends Chinese heritage with utilitarian design.
Founded in Los Angeles in 2014 by Mike Amiri; the luxury menswear label blends rock-inspired aesthetics with Californian craftsmanship.

Established in 2020 by Sonia Martínez; tailoring, craftsmanship, and construction, revealing hidden garment-making processes. Martínez studied at IED Madrid and worked at Zara, Alexander McQueen, and Phoebe Philo's Céline.

Founded by Yohji Yamamoto, who arrived in Paris from Tokyo in 1981 alongside Rei Kawakubo and upended Western ideas of tailoring with dark, fluid, deconstructed silhouettes. Still independently owned and designed by Yamamoto himself, a rarity in the industry.

shows.venue: Courtyard of Musée des Archives Nationales
shows.bio: The menswear line of System Homme, founded in Seoul; known for contemporary Korean menswear.
Founded in 1986 by Belgian designer Dries Van Noten, one of the original “Antwerp Six.” Julian Klausner became creative director in December 2024 after Van Noten’s own retirement.
Founded in Paris in 1995 by Isabel Marant, the label defines relaxed, irreverent Parisian luxury. Marant's effortless bohemian-inflected collections blend cool nonchalance with precise craftsmanship.

Founded in 1992 by Junya Watanabe (b. 1961, Fukushima), a Rei Kawakubo protégé who trained as a Comme des Garçons patternmaker. Known as a pioneer of “techno-couture,” mixing advanced fabrics with inventive draping and construction.
KML is a Saudi menswear label by co-founders and creative directors Ahmed and Razan Hassan, known for minimalist, fluid tailoring rooted in Saudi culture; it was shortlisted for the 2025 LVMH Prize.

Lazoschmidl is a German-Swedish menswear and non-binary label founded in 2014 by Andreas Schmidl and Josef Lazo, uniting fashion design with literature to create narrative-driven, body-celebrating collections.
Founded in 1889 by Jeanne Lanvin, the oldest French fashion house still in operation. Peter Copping is artistic director.
Founded in Tokyo in 1996 by Mihara Yasuhiro; the label is known for the original sole sneaker and subversive design.
New York-based menswear designer; the label explores Chicano culture and oversized tailoring.
Founded in 2017 by Reid Baker and Ines Amorim; the menswear label reinterprets American classics.
The menswear line of Comme des Garçons, founded by Rei Kawakubo in Tokyo in 1969; Homme Plus presents avant-garde menswear in Paris.
Paris-based menswear designer; known for tailored menswear with a contemporary edge.
Founded in Paris in 2012 by Pierre Mahéo; the menswear label offers timeless French wardrobe essentials.
Founded in Los Angeles in 2018 by Eli Russell Linnetz; the label blends Californian youth culture with luxury.
Paris-based menswear designer; the label explores masculinity with surgical precision.
Founded in 2014 by Demna and Guram Gvasalia; the Zurich-based label built on oversized proportions and streetwear codes. Guram Gvasalia became creative director in 2021.
Founded in Bologna in 2016 by Luca Magliano; the menswear label explores Italian provincial identity with raw tailoring.

AMC – Aldo Maria Camillo is a menswear brand founded in 2018 by Aldo Maria Camillo, a designer formerly of Valentino, Zegna and Cerruti, reinterpreting the archetypes of the male wardrobe through tailoring.

French leather goods house founded in 1837 by Thierry Hermès. Nadège Vanhee-Cybulski has been artistic director of women’s ready-to-wear since 2014, prized for a decade-long tenure of stability in an industry defined by rotation.
Founded in 1993 by Jun Takahashi in Tokyo, rooted in the city's punk and subculture scene. Takahashi remains creative director of his own label.

Kiko Kostadinov is a London label founded by Bulgarian designer Kiko Kostadinov, known for workwear, uniforms and functional details. His experimental construction reworks utilitarian references into refined, forward-thinking design.
Shanghai-based menswear designer; the label is known for deconstructed tailoring with Chinese influences.
Founded in Tokyo in 2004 by Junichi Abe; the menswear label is known for innovative pattern-making and color.
Maison Kitsuné is a Franco-Japanese lifestyle brand founded in Paris in 2002 by Gildas Loaëc and Masaya Kuroki, spanning fashion, the Kitsuné Musique record label and Café Kitsuné.
Founded in Tokyo in 2013 by Takuya Morikawa; the menswear label is known for experimental textiles.
Launched in 2002 as a collaboration between Yohji Yamamoto and Adidas; the avant-garde sportswear line blends Japanese design with athletic function.
Hed Mayner is an Israeli-born, Paris-based designer who founded his eponymous menswear label in 2015; his sculptural, oversized tailoring won the 2019 LVMH Karl Lagerfeld Prize.
SOSHIOTSUKI is a Tokyo menswear label founded in 2015 by Soshi Otsuki, fusing Japanese tradition and spirituality with modern tailoring; Otsuki won the 2025 LVMH Prize.

Tokyo menswear label founded in 2016 by self-taught designer Kiichiro Asakawa (as stein; renamed ssstein for the Fall/Winter 2024 season). Known for quiet minimalism built on precision construction and exceptional Japan-made fabrics; winner of the FASHION PRIZE OF TOKYO 2025, which this event celebrated.
Founded in Paris in 2002 by Youngmi Woo; the South Korean menswear label is known for architectural tailoring.
Founded in 1945 by Céline Vipiana as a made-to-measure children’s shoe shop in Paris. Michael Rider became creative director in 2025, succeeding Hedi Slimane.
LAD/ is a menswear label founded by designer Ladislas Mande, blending Italian tailoring with Congolese cultural references and a contemporary approach to proportion.
Founded in 1999 by Chitose Abe in Tokyo, known for “splicing” two or more garments into one hybrid piece. Abe remains creative director of her own label.
Founded in Seoul in 2018; the technical menswear label is known for deconstructed utilitarian design.
Founded in Tokyo in 2012 by Masayuki Ino; the menswear label won the 2018 LVMH Prize, known for playful subversion.
Amsterdam-based menswear designer; the label is known for oversized, deconstructed tailoring.

P. Andrade is a Brazilian menswear label led by designers Pedro Andrade and Paula Kim, merging culture, technology and sustainability; it was the first Brazilian brand on the official Paris Fashion Week calendar.
Founded in Paris in 1975 by Agnès Troublé, agnès b. is known for simple, timeless clothing — including the iconic snap cardigan. The brand's understated French style has endured as a wardrobe staple.
Founded in Tokyo in 2010 by Shinpei Yamagishi; the menswear label reimagines American classics with Japanese precision.
Founded in 1975 in Corridonia, Italy; the luxury footwear brand is known for handcrafted men's shoes.
Founded in 1986 by Dirk Bikkembergs; the Belgian-Italian sportswear brand blends fashion and football culture.

Founded in 1953 in Gallarate by Ottavio and Rosita Missoni, known for colorful zigzag-patterned knitwear. Family-run for three generations; Alberto Caliri is creative director, with Angela Missoni as president. Rosita Missoni passed away in late 2025 at age 93.
Founded in Naples in 1986; the Italian brand is known for the dachshund logo and preppy Mediterranean style.
Copenhagen label founded in 2023 by designer and creative director Martin Juncker, working between fashion, theatre, installation and performance.
Founded in 1967 by Ralph Lauren, built on an aspirational, preppy vision of American style — the polo player logo among the most recognized in fashion.
Founded in 1978 in Solomeo, Italy, by Brunello Cucinelli; the luxury house is known for cashmere and understated Italian elegance.
Italian premium denim label presented as a digital release at Milan Fashion Week for Fall/Winter 2025.
Founded in 1967 by Ralph Lauren, built on an aspirational, preppy vision of American style — the polo player logo among the most recognized in fashion.
Founded in 1985 in Italy; the outerwear brand, part of Tod's Group, is known for the 4 Ganci coat.
Founded in 1968 in Naples by Ciro Paone; the luxury menswear house is renowned for Neapolitan tailoring and handcrafted garments.
Founded in 1873 in Northampton, England; the luxury footwear maker is known for Goodyear-welted shoes, part of Prada Group since 1999.
Founded in Rome in 1945 by Nazareno Fonticoli and Gaetano Savini; the Italian menswear house is renowned for sartorial ready-to-wear and bespoke tailoring, acquired by Kering in 2011.

Italian luxury menswear tailoring house founded in Soragna in 1958 by Neapolitan tailor Raffaele Caruso. Known for "playful elegance," it pairs sartorial rigour with contemporary Italian style and manufactures for several global fashion houses.

Chinese menswear brand founded in 2016 by Yushan Li and Jun Zhou, based between Milan and Shanghai. Celebrating its 10th anniversary, Pronounce's Spring/Summer 2027 collection continued their exploration of the dialogue between Eastern heritage and contemporary design.

Founded in 1985 in Legnano by Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana, epitomizing Italian glamour and sensuality. Gabbana stepped down as chairman in late 2025 but remains co-creative director alongside Dolce.

Founded in 2009 in Milan by Massimo Giorgetti, blending traditional Italian tailoring with youthful, Technicolor sportswear codes. Giorgetti also served as creative director of Emilio Pucci from 2015-2017.

Contemporary luxury menswear brand established by Colombian designer Nicolas Martin Garcia, blending Colombian heritage with Italian craftsmanship. Its Spring/Summer 2027 "Si lo crees, lo creas – Latin Dreamers" collection marked the first Colombian brand on Milan Fashion Week's official calendar.
Founded in 1930 in Mantua, Italy; the menswear house is known for sartorial tailoring and Made in Italy quality.
Historic Italian menswear brand producing 100% Made in Italy clothing.

Founded in 2021 by Rainy Womack in Los Angeles, known for luxury streetwear blending raw emotion with handmade Italian craftsmanship. Went viral after its Paris Bag appeared on Netflix's Selling Sunset; debuted on the official Milan Fashion Week calendar in 2026.
Setchu is the menswear label of Japanese designer Satoshi Kuwata.
Paul Smith is the British fashion house founded by designer Paul Smith. The label's March 19, 2025 presentation was its Tokyo runway debut, staged under the ‘by R’ banner.
Founded in 1998 by German designer and entrepreneur Philipp Plein, known for maximalist, rhinestone-heavy luxury streetwear. Headquartered in Lugano, Switzerland.
Founded in Milan in 2007 by Marco Baldassari and Paolo Zuntini; the menswear brand is known for smart-casual luxury with Made in Italy craftsmanship.

Founded in Milan by Simone Cracker (b. 1985), who began in 2006 making accessories from upholstery materials before officially launching Simon Cracker in 2010. Built entirely on giving old and unused clothes and materials new life through patchwork and upcycling.

Hoor Al-Qasimi's Spring/Summer 2027 collection for Qasimi explores the act of making through relaxed tailoring, modular construction and an organic approach to materials. Inspired by the work of Gulf artist Hassan Sharif, the collection reflects on repetition, craftsmanship and the traces left by manual processes.
Milanese label founded in 2017, presented as a digital release at Milan Fashion Week for Fall/Winter 2025.

Founded in 1913 by Mario Prada in Milan as a leather goods shop; became a fashion house under Miuccia Prada from the 1980s on. Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons have served as co-creative directors since 2020.
Founded in 1934 in Triuggio, Italy, by Giacomo Canali; the family-owned menswear house is known for sartorial tailoring and Made in Italy craftsmanship.
London-based menswear designer Saul Nash presented his Spring/Summer 2027 collection "STANCE" during Milan Men's Fashion Week.
Founded in 1978 in Filottrano, Italy, by the Lardini brothers; the menswear brand is known for modern tailoring with artisanal details.
Historic Biella textile house founded in 1733, producing luxury fabrics and menswear.

Roots trace to a shoemaking workshop founded by Filippo Della Valle in the early 1900s in the Marche region; his grandson Diego Della Valle built it into the global Tod’s brand, best known for the hand-stitched, rubber-studded Gommino driving shoe.
Founded in 1970 in Quinto Vicentino, Italy; the menswear brand is part of the Forall group, known for refined Italian tailoring.
Milanese jewelry brand known for its charm collections.
Founded by Gimmo Etro, known for its signature paisley print. A family business: children Kean, Veronica, and Jacopo Etro have led menswear, womenswear, and accessories respectively.

shows.bio: Label by Cameroonian designer Paul Tanonkou, presented as a digital release at Milan Fashion Week for Spring/Summer 2026.

Founded in 2001 by Thom Browne in New York, built around a signature shrunken gray suit and reinventions of American tailoring. Browne remains creative director of his own label.

Founded in 1975 by Giorgio Armani, who redefined masculine and feminine elegance through deconstructed, minimalist tailoring. Armani passed away in September 2025 at age 91; his niece Silvana Armani, already his longtime design deputy, now leads ready-to-wear.

Ivorian menswear brand built around Kente cloth, its signature fabric and enduring point of departure. The brand presents its collections as intimate fashion films, making its Milan Fashion Week debut digitally for Spring/Summer 2027.
Ghana-based brand making its historic Milan Fashion Week debut with Spring/Summer 2027, presenting digitally on the official calendar.

Founded in 2018 by Christopher Akpo, SUBWAE is a Ghana-based unisex brand built around storytelling, aesthetic evolution, and sustainable design. Drawing inspiration from architecture, art, and Ghana's landscapes, the brand explores garment-making through experimentation and craftsmanship.
Founded in 2015 by Brandon Maxwell, who first came up styling and designing for Lady Gaga.

Founded in 2011 by Todd Snyder, known for reworking classic American menswear.

Genderless New York label founded in 2019 by Aaron Potts.

Founded in New York in 1997 by Andrew Rosen and Elie Tahari.

shows.bio: Los Angeles-based label launched in 2022 by Kari Vettese, drawing on her Italian heritage; worn by Charli XCX, Florence Pugh, and Kylie Jenner.

New York label founded by Christian Juul Nielsen.

Brooklyn womenswear launched in 2024 by Colleen Allen, a former menswear designer at The Row and Raf Simons’ Calvin Klein; draws on her archive of antique clothing for otherworldly collections rooted in craft, identity, and the act of getting dressed.
French house founded in 1985, known for the bandage dress.

Brooklyn design house founded in 2017 by identical twin sisters Dynasty and Soull Ogun; creates ornate jewelry, accessories, and clothing inspired by mythology, alchemy, science, and the mystical practices of their Nigerian and Dominican ancestors. The duo won the 2024 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund.

Formally established in 2022 by Kazakhstan-born founder and creative director Meruert Tolegen; known for sharp construction, strong silhouettes, and Kazakh-inflected femininity.
Founded in 2015 by Laura Kim and Fernando Garcia, who are also co-creative directors of Oscar de la Renta.

Nigerian-born, New York-based designer Teniola “Tia” Adeola founded the label in 2016 as Slashed by Tia; known for dramatic ruffles and Renaissance-inspired dresses that recast art history through a diverse, feminine lens. Fall 2025 marked ten years of the label.

Milwaukee-born, Puerto Rican-heritage designer Elena Velez (b. 1994) trained at Parsons and Central Saint Martins, known for synthesizing metalsmithing with high fashion. Named CFDA's 2022 Emerging Designer of the Year.
Label created in 2020 by Jacques Agbobly, formerly behind Black Boy Knits; celebrates West African craft and Black, queer, immigrant narratives.

Brazilian label designed by founder and creative director Patricia Bonaldi, in business for about 20 years and in the U.S. for a decade. Known for Brazilian artisan embroidery, fringe, dimensional detailing and draping across beachwear and eveningwear; the collection is manufactured in Brazil. Sold at Saks Fifth Avenue, Bloomingdale’s, Revolve and Bergdorf Goodman. Introduced footwear for fall 2026 and an eyewear collection for spring 2027.
Brooklyn label founded in 2016 by Edvin Thompson; draws on Jamaican/Caribbean heritage, New York, and migration.
Founded in 1981 by Carolina Herrera, long associated with ladylike tailoring and dramatic white shirting.
New York-based womenswear label founded by Trish Wescoat Pound, dedicated to reimagining the modern woman's closet.
Founded in 2020 by Henry Zankov in New York, known for colorful, playful knitwear. Zankov also became Diane von Furstenberg's artistic director in 2026.

Eponymous line launched in 2015 by Israeli designer Kobi Halperin; artisan detail, handcrafted embellishments, and modern femininity.

Luxury womenswear label founded in 2017 by Alexandra O’Neill; slow, made-to-order craftsmanship with celestial romanticism.
Genderless Brooklyn label founded by Tanner Richie and Fletcher Kasell; fashion alongside vintage interiors and home décor.
New York label shown by appointment during NYFW; press from 2024 identifies the designer only as Yitao.

Founded in 2012 by South African-born designer Daniella Kallmeyer in New York, known for fluid, body-conscious tailoring.
New York couture house launched in 2016 by married co-designers Anna Rose Shaheen and Anthony Cucculelli; known for intricate hand embroidery. Fall 2025 was Collection 19, “Memento Fiori.”
Namesake house founded in 1983 by Dennis Basso; known for fur, eveningwear, bridal, and accessories.

Luxury womenswear label built around the idea of forgotten traditions, founded by Stephanie Suberville and her husband Jeffrey Axford.

New York-based designer known for technology-enhanced shape engineering and fabric-first, sculptural experimentation over traditional themed collections. Named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in 2025; worn by Beyoncé and Katy Perry.

New York label founded and designed by Neil Grotzinger; known for embroidery, beadwork, altered menswear, and experimental textiles.

London-based knitwear designer known for crochet and artisanal knit pieces reworking repurposed vintage garments, deadstock yarns and sheepskin; presented through BFC's DiscoveryLAB.

Fashion brand founded by Argentine designer Nikole Tursi, creating high-quality bespoke pieces with a craft-led, artisanal approach.

New York streetwear label founded in 2010 by designer David BenDavid, known for art-driven backpacks and accessories bearing the iconic 'Shark Mouth' motif.

East London designer known for tailoring-driven collections and immersive, party-style show formats staged in nightclub and subculture-adjacent venues, often working with Savile Row-trained tailor Charlie Allen.

shows.bio: A collaboration between stylist Harry Lambert, Disney and Zara, presented on the official London Fashion Week schedule.
Central Saint Martins graduate Susan Fang is known for hand-crafted glass-bead accessories and her signature “air-weaving” technique, lacing layered materials into 3-dimensional forms.

shows.bio: Budapest-based label founded by Sandra Sándor, known for modern, versatile wardrobe staples; made its first London Fashion Week appearance with SS26.

Founded in 1856 by Thomas Burberry in Basingstoke, England; invented gabardine and popularized the trench coat. Daniel Lee has been creative director since 2022. ReBurberry Services offers repair, reproofing, and restoration for existing pieces.
Graduate showcase of the Institut Français de la Mode's Master of Arts programs, opening the Paris womenswear calendar.

KIMHËKIM is the label of creative director Kiminte Kimhekim, known for a couture-influenced identity of pearls, bows and conceptual construction. The brand reworks heritage dress codes into sculptural, highly finished pieces.

Founded in Paris in September 2020 by Victor Weinsanto, Weinsanto is a theatrical luxury label spanning ready-to-wear and couture. The house mixes humor, eccentricity and precise craftsmanship into exuberant, hyper-feminine collections.

Founded in Tokyo in 2020 by Yusuke Takahashi, CFCL creates computer-developed 3D knitwear from sustainable materials. The label's seamless, tech-driven knits offer a modern uniform of effortless precision.

Founded in Paris in 2019 by Spanish designer Abraham Ortuño Perez, Abra is an accessories-led label known for shoes, bags and surreal, spiky details. Spanish craftsmanship underpins its playful, offbeat luxury.

Founded in New York in 2013 by Patric DiCaprio and now led with co-creative director Bryn Taubensee, Vaquera is known for 'fashion fan fiction' — oversized proportions and subversive, DIY-informed design. The label blends Americana references with a downtown sensibility.

Founded in Paris in 2019 by Alphonse Maitrepierre, Maitrepierre mixes old-world fashion aesthetics with geek culture and eco-innovative materials. The house is known for theatrical, sustainability-minded collections.
Paris-based label co-founded by designer Danial Aitouganov and stylist Imruh Asha; known for bold color, playful silhouettes and a childlike spirit. 2025 LVMH Prize finalist.

The Paris couture house Dice Kayek was founded in 1992 by Turkish sisters Ece and Ayşe Ege. Known for sculptural, architectural 'modern romantic' design in luxurious fabrics, the house is led creatively by Ece.

Marie Adam-Leenaerdt launched her Brussels-based label in 2023 with precise, sculptural reinterpretations of everyday objects. Her multifunctional designs blend tailoring rigor with quiet conceptual play.
Founded in 2013 by Polish designer Magda Butrym, known for florals and body-conscious silhouettes.

Founded in Tokyo in 2010 by Maiko Kurogouchi, Mame Kurogouchi blends Japanese craft with personal memory and advanced textile technology. The label is known for poetic, meticulously engineered fabrics and elegant, wearable construction.

Mossi Traoré launched his Paris-area womenswear label in 2017 with a vision of urban contemporary couture. Pleating, drape and architectural silhouettes — often developed through artistic collaborations — define the house.
Founded in 1946 by Christian Dior; the 1947 “New Look” reshaped postwar fashion and still anchors the house's silhouette today.

Founded in Tokyo in 2003 by Kunihiko Morinaga, Anrealage explores technology and detailed patchwork to create forms unconstrained by the conventional body. The label is known for intellectually playful, shape-shifting design.

Launched in Paris in March 2021 by Vincent Garnier Pressiat, Pressiat is a no-gender label of provocative Parisian elegance. The collections fuse architecture, craft and nightlife into sensual, boundary-pushing design.
Founded in 1993 by Jun Takahashi in Tokyo, rooted in the city's punk and subculture scene. Takahashi remains creative director of his own label.

Founded in Paris in 2023 by Alain Paul and his husband Luis Philippe, ALAINPAUL is a dance-led unisex label born from Paul's ballet training and stints at Vetements and Louis Vuitton. The house is known for sculptural silhouettes, precise tailoring and collections conceived as a choreography of fabric and body.

Founded by Azzedine Alaïa, the house is celebrated for sculptural, body-conscious silhouettes and precision cutting. Pieter Mulier has been creative director since 2021, continuing Alaïa's legacy of exacting craftsmanship.

Founded in Paris in 2019 by artistic director Chloé Harrouche and CEO Ugo Bensoussan, Loulou de Saison offers timeless contemporary womenswear. The label is known for understated classics made from quality materials.
Founded in 1961 by André Courrèges, a pioneer of 1960s space-age fashion. Nicolas Di Felice was artistic director from 2020.

Founded in Kyiv in 2009 by Lilia Litkovska, Litkovska is known for architectural tailoring, deconstruction and transformable garments. The label's conceptual, sculptural pieces reflect its Ukrainian roots and avant-garde spirit.
Paris house founded in 1925 by Marcel Rochas; Alessandro Vigilante became creative director in late 2023.

Founded in New York City in 2006 by Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen, The Row is the standard-bearer of understated luxury. It is known for precise tailoring, premium materials and a quiet, exacting aesthetic.

Founded in 2018 by Charaf Tajer, Casablanca is an après-sport luxury label known for hand-painted prints and relaxed, Riviera-inflected tailoring. Tajer remains the brand's founder and creative director.

shows.debut: Julian Klausner's debut as creative director.
shows.bio: Founded in 1986 by Belgian designer Dries Van Noten, one of the original “Antwerp Six.” Julian Klausner became creative director in December 2024 after Van Noten’s own retirement.

Antwerp-trained designer Julie Kegels founded her namesake label in 2024, contrasting precision with fluidity and tradition with innovation. Her collections explore feminine archetypes through refined, sculptural construction.
Founded in 2015 by Cecilie Bahnsen in Copenhagen, known for voluminous, sculptural dresses in technical fabrics. Bahnsen remains creative director of her own label.

Founded in 2001 by Stella McCartney in London; the house has been leather- and fur-free from day one and has since developed plant-based faux fur and lab-grown vegan silk. McCartney remains creative director of her own label.

Founded in March 2021 by Ruohan Nie, Ruohan practices elevated minimalism through precise tailoring, exceptional fabrics and a neutral palette. The label's pared-back pieces emphasize cut and material over ornament.

Founded in 1996 in Stockholm by Jonny Johansson, part of a wider ACNE (“Ambition to Create Novel Expression”) creative collective spanning photography, art, and design. Johansson remains creative director.

shows.debut: Haider Ackermann's debut as creative director.
shows.bio: Founded in 2005 by American designer Tom Ford after his tenures at Gucci and Saint Laurent. Haider Ackermann is creative director, succeeding Peter Hawkings.
Founded in 1945 by Pierre Balmain, known for sculpted, glamorous tailoring. Olivier Rousteing was creative director from 2011 to November 2025.

Founded in 1952 by Gaby Aghion in Paris, known for its bohemian, romantic femininity. Chemena Kamali became creative director in October 2023 — her third stint at the house — succeeding Gabriela Hearst.

Founded in 2012 by Virgil Abloh in Milan, credited with helping bring streetwear into the luxury runway conversation. Abloh died in 2021; the brand has since been without a permanent creative director following Ib Kamara's departure.

Founded in 2018 by Caroline Hú, Reverie by Caroline Hú is known for radical romanticism, textile craft and emotional storytelling. The label's dreamlike collections merge artisanal technique with narrative depth.
Founded in 1966 by Paco Rabanne; Julien Dossena was creative director from 2013. Part of Puig.
Label listed on the official FHCM womenswear calendar for Spring/Summer 2026.
