Australian luxury womenswear brand established around 2000, known for tactile, natural fabrics and enduring, unconventional design.

shows.debut: AFW debut (solo runway, per frankie).
shows.bio: Naarm/Melbourne menswear label founded by Gooreng Gooreng and South Sea Islander designer Juanita Page in 2021, weaving contemporary design with cultural storytelling.
Byron Bay label founded by Laura May Gibbs with her sister and collaborator Hannah Gibbs, combining art, sustainability and functionality across fashion and activewear.

Australian made and owned luxury ready-to-wear label founded by Co-Founder and Creative Director Gabriella Pereira; launched at AFW 2021; Sydney-designed and locally made in limited runs, championing masterful tailoring and slow fashion.
Australian tailoring and lifestyle label founded by husband-and-wife co-creative directors Joe Farage and Katy Farage.
Australian fashion house founded in 2008 by Adrian Norris and Edwina Forest, dedicated to raw beauty, tough femininity and effortless cool, bridging coastal and urban dressing.

Sydney-based fashion and textiles designer who launched his eponymous label in 2021; known for emotionally charged garments blurring poetry, digital culture and physical craft, with text-laden prints and sculptural silhouettes; named Emerging Designer of the Year at the 2023 Australian Fashion Laureate.

Sustainable First Nations womenswear label founded in 2018 by Wiradjuri entrepreneur Denni Francisco; collaborates with First Nations artists to transpose artworks onto premium-quality garments — Ngali translates to ‘we’ or ‘us’ in several Aboriginal languages.
Australian womenswear designer known for fluid draping and precise tailoring.
Label by Dubrovnik-born, Sydney-based designer Karla Špetić, who founded her eponymous line in 2008; known for soft tailoring and a romantic tension between feminine fabrics and sharper silhouettes.
Sydney womenswear label established in April 2012 by sisters Beth and Tessa MacGraw, known for directional prints, playful femininity and strong runway storytelling.
Contemporary Australian womenswear label founded in 2012.
Experimental, non-gendered fashion house founded by Jordan Gogos, centred on co-design, upcycling, textile innovation and sculptural wearable art.

Sydney-based eponymous label established in 2003; custom made-to-order fine-art collections hand painted by the designer onto ethically sourced eco-cotton, known for masterful drape, intelligent silhouettes and artful colour.
Sydney prêt-à-couture designer known for architectural silhouettes, structured tailoring, fluid drapery and hand embellishment.
Sydney demi-couture label founded in 2014 by Katie-Louise and Lil Nicol-Ford; ethically made to order, working with remnant textiles and queer-history narratives.
Boteh was founded in October 2020 by Amelia Mather; the resortwear label is built on artisan prints, wearable design, thoughtful production and relaxed Australian–Mediterranean references.
Gomeroi label founded by Colleen Tighe-Johnson that translates commissioned Gomeroi artworks and Dreaming stories into one-off garments, alongside a youth-development social enterprise.
Label by Sydney designer Hannah Teresa, known for dark romanticism and elevated wardrobe staples; stocked at Reborne Shop, the independent Sydney retail space she also directs.

Miimi + Jiinda is a First Nations fashion and art label founded by Gumbaynggirr, Bundjalung and Dunghutti artist and designer Melissa Greenwood with her mother, master weaver Lauren Jarrett; it centres matriarchal storytelling and Country.

Permanent Vacation was founded by Melbourne designer Claire Louise Smith; the label rejects conventional seasonal collections in favour of numbered Projects, made locally in Melbourne in timeless small runs.

Liandra is a swim and resortwear label founded and creatively directed by Yolngu designer Liandra Gaykamangu; its reversible pieces feature hand-drawn cultural storytelling prints and recycled and regenerated materials.

Romance Was Born was founded in Sydney in 2005 by Anna Plunkett and Luke Sales; the fashion house is known for craftsmanship, vivid prints, embellishment and collaborations with artists across fashion, theatre and art.
aaizél was established by Melbourne designer Minhee Jo in 2013; the label uses consciously sourced fabric, in-house cutting with minimum-waste methods, handwork and juxtaposed textiles.

Connor O'Grady is an Australian womenswear designer based in London, known for sculptural silhouettes, historical references and craftsmanship; a 2023 London College of Fashion womenswear graduate, he was shortlisted for the 2024 British Vogue × BMW Future Creators competition and presented at AFW 2025 as a Vogue Vanguard designer.
Ruby Pedder is a Sydney-based designer whose grown-up, romantic yet practical womenswear is designed to be treasured; she was one of seven designers in the 2025 Vogue Vanguard showcase.
Emily Watson is a Melbourne-based emerging designer who was one of seven designers selected for the 2025 Vogue Vanguard next-generation runway at Australian Fashion Week.
Brendan Plummer is an Australian emerging designer whose work explores conceptual themes through corporate uniforms, sculptural and crumpled forms, prints and avant-garde references.
Ethan Bergersen is an emerging Australian designer who was one of seven designers selected for the 2025 Vogue Vanguard next-generation runway at Australian Fashion Week.
Samuel Lewis is an emerging Australian designer who was one of seven designers selected for the 2025 Vogue Vanguard next-generation runway at Australian Fashion Week.

Founded in 2001 by Central Saint Martins graduates Hokuto Katsui and Nao Yagi, mintdesigns is a Tokyo women's label known for bold prints, patterns and color. The duo approaches fashion as product design.
HOUGA is a women's label founded in 2019 by designer Moe Ishida. Its poetic philosophy centers on unveiling hidden gifts.

Petit Bateau is a French clothing and underwear house whose origins date to Pierre Valton's 1893 hosiery factory in Troyes. The house became trans-generational with the introduction of adult collections alongside its classic children's wear.
Established under the pillings name in 2020 by Ryota Murakami, the Tokyo label centers on hand-knit women's ready-to-wear.
Launched in 2020 by designer Emi Funayama, FETICO is a Tokyo women's label known for corsetry, sheer fabrics, cutouts and body-conscious silhouettes.
Founded in 2004 by designer Yoshio Kubo, yoshiokubo is a Tokyo men's ready-to-wear label emphasizing original patterns and details.
Founded in 2013 by Hideaki Yoshihara and Yukiko Ode, HYKE reworks vintage military and workwear references into refined womenswear.
Founded in 2012 by Takafumi Sekine, meagratia is a Tokyo men's and unisex label built on a fusion of history and a present-day sensibility.
NON TOKYO is the Tokyo label of designer Shun Nakagawa, whose Fall/Winter 2025 collection was presented on the official Rakuten Fashion Week Tokyo schedule on March 18, 2025.

KANEMASA PHIL. is the original brand of a Wakayama-based circular-knit manufacturer with more than 50 years of production history. The label is known for advanced high-gauge knitting and artisan operation of the machinery.
The house behind TAE ASHIDA debuted in 1991, and Jun Ashida became its creative director in 2018. It presents modern high fashion that preserves the founding philosophy of “Elegant and Practical.”
HUMMEL 00 is helmed by designer Masanori Morikawa, combining hummel's sportswear and function heritage with technology and modern design.
Founded by Viviano Sue — China-born, US-raised and Tokyo-based since 2008 — VIVIANO moved from bridal and couture into prêt-à-porter.
Founded in 2014 by designer Lim Asafuji, pays des fées is a Tokyo ready-to-wear label built on a ‘strange and cute’ sensibility.
Founded in 2021 by Tokio Kimura, tokio is a punk-rooted Tokyo menswear label; Kimura's background includes vintage repair and remaking.
Founded in 2011 by Sho Iwata and Hiroshi Takizawa, tiit tokyo is a lyrical women's ready-to-wear label.

shows.debut: Paul Smith's Tokyo runway debut, presented under the ‘by R’ banner.
shows.bio: Paul Smith is the British fashion house founded by designer Paul Smith. The label's March 19, 2025 presentation was its Tokyo runway debut, staged under the ‘by R’ banner.
Established in 2015 by designer Keisuke Yoshida, KEISUKEYOSHIDA is an experimental, deconstructionist Tokyo label.
Founded in 2019 by designer Satoru Sasaki, the label balances feminine and masculine design across men's and women's ready-to-wear. It received the TOKYO FASHION AWARD 2025.

Heaven Tanudiredja launched his namesake label in 2007 after training at the Royal Academy of Fine Arts Antwerp and working with John Galliano, Dior Haute Couture and Dries Van Noten. Now Bali-based, the label creates sculptural, architectural, handcrafted garments.
BASICKS is the Tokyo label of designer Masanori Morikawa.
YOUJIYOUNG is a Korean label founded in 2002, combining classic fashion, contemporary deconstruction, costume and performance work, and cultural collaborations.

shows.venue: TODA HALL & CONFERENCE TOKYO HALL A
shows.bio: Founded in 2010 by Keisuke Nagami, HATRA is a unisex project connecting fashion and digital technology.
Founded in 2005 by Koji Sato, WIZZARD makes hybrid urban wear based on a ‘RE-MIXING’ concept, drawing on music, art and film as recurring sources.

Launched in 2022 from a corporate-uniform company, HIDESIGN is led by chief designer Hideo Yoshii and brand director Souta Yamaguchi. Functionality and extreme-condition workwear inform the label's designs.
Launched in 2022 by designer Nakajima, TELMA follows his tenure at Dries Van Noten and Issey Miyake.

shows.debut: The label's first runway on the official Rakuten Fashion Week Tokyo schedule.
shows.venue: TODA HALL & CONFERENCE TOKYO HALL A
shows.bio: Founded in 2021 by River Garam Jang and Nobuhiko Kohama, RIV NOBUHIKO applies couture handwork to women's ready-to-wear.
Directed by KOJI since 2017 with T$UYO$HI and KATSUMA, MSML is a music-rooted label fusing 1990s hardcore Americana, streetwear and high fashion.
Founded in 2014 by former professional ballet dancer Chika Kisada, the namesake label combines ballet elegance with punk energy.
Launched under the KAMIYA name in 2023 by Koji Kamiya, the menswear label draws on vintage and archive references with damage processing.
Launched in 2023 by Shunta Sakai, paratrait follows his graduation from Bunka and Istituto Marangoni London and womenswear experience at Alexander McQueen and Burberry.
Launched in 2015, TAN is a knitwear-centered Tokyo label working across varied knitting techniques.
Founded in 2019 by Harunobu Murata after work at John Richmond and Jil Sander, the label makes luxury womenswear combining Italian and Japanese materials and techniques.

shows.debut: Debut season under the FURUMAU name, evolved from CHONO for Fall/Winter 2025.
shows.bio: FURUMAU is the women's ready-to-wear label of designer Wataru Nakazono, evolved from CHONO beginning with the Fall/Winter 2025 season.
Keiko Nishiyama is a London College of Fashion-educated textile and fashion designer, creating original textiles featuring imagined flora and fauna.
Founded in 2021 by Tatsuya Tamada, Tamme is a Tokyo menswear label mixing military and formal categories.

shows.debut: The label's first runway show, presented September 1, 2025.
shows.bio: Founded in 2023 by Yuka Kimura, mukcyen is a Tokyo women's ready-to-wear label drawing on film, literature, human nature and time.

shows.debut: Nagonstans' Tokyo runway debut, September 1, 2025.
shows.bio: Nagonstans is the Tokyo label led by designer Mizuki Ueda. Its September 1, 2025 presentation marked the label's Tokyo runway debut.
ANCELLM is the men's ready-to-wear and accessories label of designer Kazuya Yamachika, exploring aging, changing tones and textures.

shows.brand: Bench Design Awards: Philippine Fashion Now
shows.bio: The Bench Design Awards is a competition platform for emerging Filipino designers. Its September 2, 2025 showcase at Shibuya Hikarie featured STEPHVERANO, nadalē and Peach.Garde.

Global Fashion Collective is a Vancouver Fashion Management platform launched in 2017 to showcase emerging designers on international runways. The first of two September 2, 2025 showcases presented emerging international designers on the official Tokyo schedule.

Global Fashion Collective is a Vancouver Fashion Management platform launched in 2017 to showcase emerging designers on international runways. The second of two September 2, 2025 showcases presented emerging international designers on the official Tokyo schedule.
HUMMEL 00 is helmed by designer Masanori Morikawa, combining hummel's sportswear and function heritage with technology and modern design.
Founded in 2019 by Harunobu Murata after work at John Richmond and Jil Sander, the label makes luxury womenswear combining Italian and Japanese materials and techniques.
Founded in 2004 by designer Yoshio Kubo, yoshiokubo is a Tokyo men's ready-to-wear label emphasizing original patterns and details.

SEIVSON is a Taiwanese womenswear label founded in 2017 by Tzu Chin Shen (Jill Shen). Its design centers on storytelling across gender, culture and borders, with balance and imbalance as central themes.
Founded in 1955 by milliner Akio Hirata, HAUTE MODE HIRATA is a Tokyo millinery house. Its September 3, 2025 show presented 31 hats at Shibuya Hikarie, honoring the centenary of Akio Hirata's birth.
Established under the pillings name in 2020 by Ryota Murakami, the Tokyo label centers on hand-knit women's ready-to-wear.
Launched in 2020 by designer Emi Funayama, FETICO is a Tokyo women's label known for corsetry, sheer fabrics, cutouts and body-conscious silhouettes.
TSUMORI CHISATO is the namesake label of designer Chisato Tsumori. Its September 4, 2025 show marked the label's 35th anniversary.
Marronnier College of Fashion Design presented its 2026 Spring/Summer collection on the official Rakuten Fashion Week Tokyo schedule on September 4, 2025.
Directed by KOJI since 2017 with T$UYO$HI and KATSUMA, MSML is a music-rooted label fusing 1990s hardcore Americana, streetwear and high fashion.
Founded in 2005 by Gaku Tsuyoshi, FDMTL is a Tokyo denim-focused label using boro-style patchwork, sashiko, washes and handcraft.

shows.brand: Ph Mode × Tyo By Mff (manila Fashion Forward)
shows.bio: Manila Fashion Forward began in 2014 and rebranded under the PH MODE × TYO name in 2025. Its September 5, 2025 presentation joined three emerging Filipino designers and one Japanese designer, pairing Filipino artwork with Japanese textile-printing technology.
Launched in 2018 by Mitsuru Okazaki after the Ito Garment Research Institute and Yohji Design Institute and pattern-production experience, the label makes men's and women's ready-to-wear.
Founded in 2014 by former professional ballet dancer Chika Kisada, the namesake label combines ballet elegance with punk energy.

Founded in 1999 by designer Norio Surikabe, support surface is a Tokyo women's ready-to-wear label. Surikabe trained in Italy — assisting at ROMEO GIGLI and serving as chief designer of NN STUDIO at 10 Corso Como — before returning to Japan in 2003.
Founded by Viviano Sue — China-born, US-raised and Tokyo-based since 2008 — VIVIANO moved from bridal and couture into prêt-à-porter.

Founded in 2019 by Central Saint Martins knitwear graduate Yueqi Qi after work in Chanel's embroidery atelier, the label makes narrative womenswear centered on embroidery, glass beads, Chinese craft and innovative textiles.
WISHARAWISH is the Thai label of designer Wisharawish Akarasantisook, creating wearable art through technical experiments, handicraft, geometric repetition and Thai craft traditions.
Founded in 2020 by self-taught designer Kenta Orimi, ORIMI is a Harajuku-rooted menswear label with a sleek gothic direction, built on the concept ‘Superfine garment for all the outsiders.’
Founded in 2018 by designer Ana Luisa Fernandes, Aluf builds womenswear around volume, curves and a neutral palette, with an ongoing research practice in innovative textiles.

Alexandre Herchcovitch launched his eponymous label in 1992 and became one of Brazil's most internationally known designers, pairing subversive, youth-culture-inflected design with precise construction and his signature skull motif.
Normando, led by Marco Normando and Emídio Contente, draws on Amazonian references, tailoring and regional materials to dress a contemporary northern-Brazilian identity.

shows.debut: SPFW debut
shows.bio: Leandro Castro makes his SPFW debut with experimental tailoring built from hybrid technologies and discarded or industrial-residue materials, blending technological, ancestral and artisanal making.
Founded in Fortaleza in 1982 by Lino Villaventura, the label is known for sculptural, heavily textured womenswear; Régis Vieira has been its creative director since 1999.
Dario Mittmann entered the SPFW lineup in October 2024 with a streetwear-inflected, futurist design language rooted in illustration and youth culture.
Weider Silveiro founded his eponymous brand in 2002, working an urban minimalism that mixes streetwear, tailoring and Northeastern Brazilian hand techniques.
Founded in 2013 by Heloisa Strobel, Reptilia designs architecture-led forms that prioritize functionality and a lower-waste production process.
Led was founded by designer Célio Dias, working manual Brazilian techniques through jeanswear and street-inflected tailoring.
Founded in 2004 and owned and creatively directed by Fábio Souza, À La Garçonne works upcycling, reuse and ressignification of existing garments into new pieces.
João Pimenta is a Brazilian menswear designer known for sophisticated, avant-garde tailoring that expands the conventions of masculine dress.
Led by Hisan Silva and Pedro Batalha, Dendezeiro makes inclusive, genderless fashion centered on Black and Brazilian identity.

shows.debut: SPFW debut
shows.bio: MNMAL, founded and creatively directed by Flavio Gamaum, makes its SPFW debut with an essentialist concept and sophisticated aesthetic built on minimalism and denim, with a sustainability concern.
Pernambuco-born Walério Araújo designs around intentional excess — shine, sensuality and a theatrical, pop-inflected femininity.
Handred, by André Namitala, works handcraft, embroidery and textile research through Brazilian references.
Patricia Viera is an established Brazilian leather specialist known for handmade treatments and tracked, certified leathers.
Piet, founded by Pedro Andrade, makes streetwear that combines tailoring, sport, utility and technology; the N59 show marked the brand's return to the SPFW lineup.
João Pimenta opened SPFW N60 at the centenary Biblioteca Mário de Andrade with 'Tropicalizando', a summer 2026 collection of light, tropicalized tailoring in vivid color.

Gloria Coelho's brand began in 1974 and is known for modern, minimalist tailoring worked in technical materials; the N60 show, staged at Estação Júlio Prestes, celebrated roughly 50 years of the label.

Ronaldo Fraga is a Brazilian designer whose narrative-led work centers culture, memory, handcraft and social histories; the N60 show at the Museu da Língua Portuguesa marked his return to the SPFW runway after six years.

Flavia Aranha began her São Paulo brand in 2009 and is a reference in purpose-driven fashion, working natural dyes, organic and agroecological inputs and artisan partnerships; N60 marked her return to the SPFW lineup.
Patricia Viera is an established Brazilian leather specialist known for handmade treatments and tracked, certified leathers.

Forca Studio was created by Vivian Rivaben and Silvio de Marchi and makes urban, experimental work informed by club and subcultural codes; the N60 show staged a parachuting-inspired presentation at Campo de Marte.
shows.cd: Vivian Rivaben and Silvio de Marchi

shows.bio: Lilly Sarti was founded in 2006 by sisters Lilly and Renata Sarti and designs versatile, contemporary womenswear with a relaxed elegance.
Founded in 2004 and owned and creatively directed by Fábio Souza, À La Garçonne works upcycling, reuse and ressignification of existing garments into new pieces.
Meninos Rei was created by Céu and Júnior Rocha and makes Afro-Bahian fashion from African textiles, patchwork, ancestry and street references.
Founded in Fortaleza in 2017, Marina Bitu leads the design of her eponymous label, which channels Northeastern culture through plissé, natural materials and regional handwork.
Leandro Castro works experimental tailoring built from hybrid technologies and discarded or industrial-residue materials, blending technological, ancestral and artisanal making.
Catarina Mina is a Ceará-based label founded and directed by Celina Hissa, built on collaborative artisan production — especially crochet — with traceability and women's economic empowerment.
Dario Mittmann works a streetwear-inflected, futurist design language rooted in illustration and youth culture.
Handred, by André Namitala, works handcraft, embroidery and textile research through Brazilian references; the N60 collection 'Baila' moved from dusk into night in richly embroidered surfaces.
Sau is a Brazilian beach and resort label begun in 2021, designing clean, multifunctional swim and resort pieces.
Foz is an Alagoas label led by Antônio Castro, working tailoring, craft and popular Brazilian and Northeastern culture; the N60 collection turned childhood memories into poetry.
Normando, led by Marco Normando and Emídio Contente, draws on Amazonian references, tailoring and regional materials to dress a contemporary northern-Brazilian identity.

The Sou de Algodão movement — an initiative of Abrapa, the Brazilian Association of Cotton Producers — presented its fourth SPFW show, 'Trajetórias': 36 all-black looks by six guest designers made from certified, traceable Brazilian cotton through the SouABR responsible-cotton program.
Founded in 2018, Bold Strap is a queer-focused label that grew from underwear and fetishwear into full clothing collections.

shows.venue: Sala de Ensaios do Teatro Municipal
shows.bio: Alexandre Herchcovitch launched his eponymous label in 1992 and became one of Brazil's most internationally known designers, pairing subversive, youth-culture-inflected design with precise construction and his signature skull motif.

Rafael Caetano is a São Paulo designer and fashion teacher who showed for nearly a decade at Casa de Criadores before joining the SPFW lineup in 2023; his fluid menswear explores gender through pleating, crochet and deconstructed tailoring.

Cria Costura is a creative accelerator run by the City of São Paulo's economic development secretariat with IN-MODE, training sewing talents from the city's peripheries; under stylist and consultant Jefferson de Assis, students present pieces made with zero-waste techniques.

Ateliê Mão de Mãe is a social-impact crochet label involving 89 women — many of them single mothers — from riverside communities in Salvador, turning hand crochet into income and professional opportunity.
Founded by designer Mônica Sampaio, Santa Resistência makes Afro-Brazilian fashion with slow, conscious and fair production.
Led by Hisan Silva and Pedro Batalha, Dendezeiro makes inclusive, genderless fashion centered on Black and Brazilian identity.

shows.debut: SPFW debut
shows.bio: Uó is Marcelo Sommer's new upcycling brand — work he has done since 2019 — ressignifying old and remnant garments into playful, authorial, low-impact looks; the N60 show was its SPFW debut.

Born in Cape Verde and based in Rio de Janeiro since 1994, Angela Brito created her eponymous brand in 2014, joining tradition and vanguard through handmade pieces that reframe African aesthetics; the N60 show was her first in an external venue, the Centro Cultural São Paulo.
David Lee is a Ceará designer who debuted on the SPFW runway in 2023, translating Northeastern identity through craft — crochet, popular-market imagery and bold print.

shows.debut: SPFW debut
shows.bio: Davi Ramos is a Brazilian hatter and stylist; the N60 show was his SPFW debut with his first clothing collection — theatrical, authorial looks in noble atelier fabrics that dialogue with his headpieces and reference 1980s and 1990s fashion.
Amir Slama is a major Brazilian beachwear designer, formerly of Rosa Chá; the N60 show marked his return to the SPFW runway with a review of his 35-year career.

Fauve is the brand of designer Clara Pasqualini, from Rio Grande do Sul; it debuted on the SPFW runway in 2024 with collections that turn family memory — wine, wood, porcelain — into unconventional volumes and transparencies.
Led was founded by designer Célio Dias, working manual Brazilian techniques through jeanswear and street-inflected tailoring.

Gustavo Silvestre is a Pernambuco-born designer trained in Italy whose crochet-based work uses reclaimed materials; he also leads Ponto Firme, the social project teaching crochet to inmates at the Adriano Marrey penitentiary in Guarulhos since 2015.
Weider Silveiro founded his eponymous brand in 2002, working an urban minimalism that mixes streetwear, tailoring and Northeastern Brazilian hand techniques.
Mercado Livre's special SPFW project brings a curated selection of fashion and accessories sold on the marketplace to the runway, connecting e-commerce with the fashion-week stage.

Apartamento 03 is a Minas Gerais brand by Luiz Claudio that debuted at SPFW in 2015; its clean, feminine collections carry a barroco mineiro sensibility in cutouts, appliqués and embroidery, often playing with gender-fluid shirting.
Martins is the brand of designer Tom Martins, focused on oversized pieces; it debuted at SPFW in 2023.

Senseaweek is a label that presented its Spring/Summer 2026 collection at Shanghai Fashion Week, where its styling used belts and neckpieces — chokers to minimal chains — layered as visual elements.
Climate Project is an American newcomer label that made its debut at Shanghai Fashion Week with Spring/Summer 2026, presenting the collection titled "Act 1" in Xintiandi.

TRIP&CO is the sub-brand of Chinese functional-fashion label TRICKCOO, led by designer Huang Junxun (Hugo). Its designs carry the group's "functional fashion" positioning — fusing outdoor-ready performance, retro sport and female strength, as seen in the 2024 "Battle Angel" presentation built on SORONA bio-based fabrics.

AS Dalio is a Beijing-born fashion brand founded in 2022, known for power dressing through bold silhouettes, rich materials and equestrian drama — armor-like coats, sharp tailoring, sheer overlays and East-meets-West references.

Ivan Yong Couture is a bridal and couture brand founded in 2019 by Malaysian designer Ivan Yong, launching its first couture collection in 2020. Its design concept is rooted in installation art, combining top fabrics, hand-set bead embroidery, antique French lace and Swarovski crystal with three-dimensional tailoring for a delicate, luxurious aesthetic.

RuirUiruI is a label whose Spring/Summer 2026 collection, "Triple Moon," explored transformation through the lunar cycle — moving from restrained minimalist oversized suiting to sequinned bustier gowns, reworking athletic elements like drawstrings and jersey through couture techniques. Its Shanghai Fashion Week runway debut was the Spring/Summer 2023 "Dragon Reborn" collection.

XU ZHI is the luxury fashion brand founded in London in 2015 by designer Xuzhi Chen, a Central Saint Martins womenswear graduate who previously worked at J.W. Anderson and Craig Green. Known for material reconstruction and signature fringe-and-braiding textile techniques, the label’s Spring/Summer 2026 show at Shanghai Fashion Week marked its tenth anniversary.

SHUSHU/TONG is the Shanghai-based womenswear label founded in 2015 by designers Liushu Lei and Yutong Jiang, London College of Fashion graduates who previously worked at Simone Rocha and Gareth Pugh. Known for a subversive girly aesthetic of bows, ruffles and dark romance, the label closed the Spring/Summer 2026 Shanghai Fashion Week edition with its tenth-anniversary showcase.

Founded in 2018, Shanghai label Hidemi makes simple, comfortable clothing for a relaxed and free lifestyle, with a store on Yanqing Road. Its collections emphasize minimalist outerwear and workwear built on simple silhouettes, often detailed with asymmetry.

Evvly is a Shanghai label known for rebellious styles and innovative sustainable materials. Its designs fuse traditional Chinese silhouettes and motifs — red fabric bundles, mandarin collars, frog fastenings — with digitally inspired exaggeration, screen-saturated colour and cosplay aesthetics.

Zouping is a label that presented its Spring/Summer 2026 collection on the Shanghai Fashion Week runway. Its menswear and womenswear range from sheer field jackets, shorts and boots to ethereal white suiting and burgundy evening ensembles, with belts and neckpieces layered as visual elements.

Founded in 2017 by Central Saint Martins MA Fashion graduate Li Gong, 8on8 is a Shanghai-based menswear label combining sportswear, traditional tailoring, retro-futurism and surrealism. It celebrated its eighth anniversary at Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026 with the collection "RUNNER THE DREAMER," built around running culture — technical fabric and heritage craft, hand-pleated dresses and embroidery clashing with neon windbreakers, plus a KEEN Jasper footwear collaboration.

jnby by JNBY is the kidswear line of Chinese designer brand house JNBY Group, one of its three younger brands alongside CROQUIS and LESS. The group builds its brands on the philosophy "Just Naturally Be Yourself," targeting middle- and upper-income customers who express individuality through fashion.

Hacchic Couture is a Vietnamese bridal and couture house founded and led by Nguyen Thi Tra Linh (Tra Linh), dressing brides in more than 40 countries. First joining Shanghai Fashion Week in October 2023, it returned for Spring/Summer 2026 with "Lunar Fracture," an avant-garde bridal collection exploring beauty within imperfection through the moon's stillness and distance.

Eenk is a Seoul fashion label founded by designer Hyemee Lee, known for its "Letter Project" — each collection organized around a single letter of the alphabet as its conceptual framework. Its narrative designs blend vintage and classic references with structural forms, unconventional colour and Korean details, and the brand has shown at New York and Paris Fashion Weeks.

FORDARE presented its Spring/Summer 2026 collection, "Romance in the 21st Century," at Shanghai Fashion Week. Lace is layered with manga-inspired graphics in sporty silhouettes, with slogan T-shirts reading "plastic relationship," "eternal love" and "best woman" commenting on modern dating, alongside a 3D-printed corset and a ceramic-accessory collaboration with label it doesn't matter.

Marie Elie Paris is a womenswear label known for lace and silk two-piece sets, positioned as a designer brand on resale markets with a made-in-China line. The label appears on the Shanghai Fashion Week calendar across multiple seasons, including Spring/Summer 2026 and Fall/Winter 2026-27.

THIS ONE is a designer label that staged its Spring/Summer 2026 show at the New Bund 31 performing arts center during Shanghai Fashion Week. New Bund 31 in Shanghai's Qiantan district was one of the season's official landmark venues alongside XINTIANDI and SUHE HAUS.

Stivanano is an Italian fashion label that presents on the Shanghai Fashion Week calendar as part of the season's international designer contingent. Following its Spring/Summer 2026 show, the label returned for the Fall/Winter 2026-27 edition.

woobaby is a childrenswear label that presented its Spring/Summer 2026 collection at Shanghai Fashion Week, appearing within the event's dedicated KIDSWEAR children's segment. No public brand biography or official website could be verified.

Croyez is a menswear label producing graphic streetwear with French-text motifs, including satin jackets, sweaters, shirts and T-shirts sold under its @croyezhomme channel. The label presented its Spring/Summer 2026 collection at Shanghai Fashion Week.

Rico Lee is a China/Hong Kong label founded in 2012 whose ethos is "Beautiful technology." It builds a bridge between technology and fashion by design to create functional clothing that fits everyday life.

Rizhao Kids (日着kids) is a Chinese childrenswear label that presented its Spring/Summer 2026 collection at Shanghai Fashion Week within the event's dedicated KIDSWEAR children's segment. No public brand biography, official website, or show time could be verified.

Camey Liu is a New York-based semi-couture designer and Parsons graduate who blends classical silhouettes, futuristic design and sustainable materials. She interned at Dior and Marchesa and founded her label from a family tailoring background.

J Rureminds is a womenswear label founded in 2021 that combines minimalist silhouettes with three-dimensional tailoring. Guided by the philosophy "Define the Confidence," it creates practical, design-conscious wardrobes for women.

Oude Waag is a Shanghai-based label founded in 2017 by designer Jingwei Yin, who studied at Central Saint Martins and the Royal College of Art and interned for Haider Ackermann; its name is Dutch for "Old Weigh House," after an Antwerp street. Its Spring/Summer 2026 collection, "Mirror, Mirror," explored resilient, fluid contemporary femininity through silk and velvet gowns with architectural cut-outs, jersey satin, and washed cargo trousers and jackets.

Comme Moi is the Shanghai-based label of former Chinese supermodel Lu Yan, who worked with Dior, Gucci, Lanvin and Alexander McQueen before retiring from modelling to found her own brand. Known for relaxed-luxe, wearable, logo-free pieces, the label opened a Neri&Hu-designed flagship store in Shanghai's Donghu Hotel.

Zita Tan is the London-based eponymous label of Beijing-born designer Tianyi Tan, launched in 2023 after her Central Saint Martins MA; its surrealist designs fuse 3D printing and experimental materials like resin and feather with soft knits to evoke marine shell forms (fzine; East Pavilion). For SHFW SS26 she made her ready-to-wear debut with the ocean-inspired ‘Three Tides’ collection, shown with archaic-marine motifs and futuristic armor-like cutouts (Hypebae; FashionUnited).

UTO 悠途 is a Chinese functional outdoor apparel label known for performance base layers and sportswear engineered for warmth, moisture management and movement (360doc product guide). It presented on the Shanghai Fashion Week SS26 runway on October 12, 2025.

Movous is a Chinese fashion label specializing in wedding dresses, associated with supermodel-turned-designer Chen Lu (China Culture/China Daily). It has shown multiple seasons on the Shanghai Fashion Week runway (ModemOnline).
港岛七公主 LuckySeven is a childrenswear label that staged a show during Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026 (official SHFW schedule).

AO YES is a contemporary label founded by Austin Wang and Yansong Liu that debuted at Shanghai Fashion Week in 2023, reinterpreting traditional Chinese dress through Eastern history, philosophy and craftsmanship (Fashion Asia HK; Clothbase).
SUNCUN 三寸盛京 is a Chinese design label by Yan Zhang that preserves traditional Chinese fabrics, embroidery and craftsmanship through contemporary reinterpretation (JT Dapper; Pynck).
LZC Jasper is a design label that staged a runway show during Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026 (official SHFW schedule).
Lacerta is the label of designer Sihui Wang; for SHFW SS26 it presented a nostalgic, romantic collection referencing Art Nouveau, boho-chic and Barcelona’s Catalan lifestyle (FashionUnited; Pynck).

HEMU 荷木 is a Shanghai-born original designer brand founded in 2010, built around an Oriental, humanist and Zen-inflected minimalist aesthetic spanning garments, tea, incense, homewares and books (解放日报; Dezeen).

ACMEITEM 爱棵米 is a Ningbo outdoor-apparel label selling parent-child quick-dry and casual clothing, owned by Ningbo Incessantly Outdoor Clothing Co., Ltd. (retail listings; USPTO records). It staged a childrenswear show at SHFW SS26 on October 12, 2025 (official SHFW schedule).
Gaofan Kids is the children’s line of Gaofan, the Chinese premium down-jacket brand founded by Wu Kunming in 2004 and focused on high-end goose-down apparel (DoNews; 21世纪经济报道).
Maison Wenēe is a design label that has presented multiple seasons on the Shanghai Fashion Week runway, including SS26 on October 12, 2025 (ModemOnline; official SHFW schedule).

Yirantian is the eponymous Shanghai label founded in 2014 by London College of Fashion graduate Yirantian Guo, known for precise tailoring, fabric craftsmanship and refined silhouettes for urban women (official site; Grazia). For SS26 she explored a dialogue between sharpness and softness, contrasting neutral suiting with powdery pastels (Vogue/MWN).

Letoii Atelier is a couture house that debuted at Shanghai Fashion Week in 2023 with its 2024 ‘Luminous Realm’ collection, defined by hand-sewn crystal embroidery, elaborate detailing and luxurious materials inspired by light and shadow (official site).

TUYUE 涂月 is an independent designer brand founded in 2008 with an art-inflected identity; designer Yang Yingying treats clothing as artistic expression, developing a restrained, literary Chinese aesthetic through fluid robes and fine fabrics rather than overt body emphasis (新民晚报).

Thanh Huong Bui is a Vietnamese designer who made her Chinese runway debut at Shanghai Fashion Week with the Spring/Summer 2026 collection. Her show featured embellished eveningwear, including a pagoda-shaped mini dress.

Lixi Couture is a couture label whose designs center on elegant evening and bridal gowns with delicate lace and embellishment. It showed at Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026, taking the runway at New Bund 31 on October 13, 2025.
YOUTOPIA (吐桃盛典) is a presentation listed on the official Shanghai Fashion Week schedule, shown during the Spring/Summer 2026 edition on October 13, 2025. It is a recurring scheduled show of the week.

We Prive presented its Spring/Summer 2026 collection at Shanghai Fashion Week, working with subtle Chinese aesthetics rendered in silk, cascading chiffon, embroidery and tulle. The collection featured floral-garland scarf draping and transparent sequin-lace pieces.
Douyin Fashion Trend is a fashion-trend presentation staged by Douyin, the short-video platform operated by ByteDance, during Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026.

Barbie by xVESSEL is a collaboration between footwear label xVESSEL and Barbie, presented during Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026. xVESSEL, led by Van Ness Wu, is rooted in deconstructionism and vulcanized sneaker craftsmanship, with its narrative beginning in 2017.

Coco&Ray is a handmade childrenswear label based in Shenyang, founded by German designer and entrepreneur Barbara. The brand made its Shanghai Fashion Week debut in April 2021 and returned to the week with a new collection for Spring/Summer 2026.

Awaylee is a womenswear label founded in 2012 by Wei Li, blending Chinese folk art, femininity, heritage and sustainability with craftsmanship. Designed in Los Angeles and crafted in China, the brand is led by creative director Sue-Ann San.

Lafine Paris is a bridal couture label known for luxurious wedding gowns with hand embroidery, lace and dramatic princess silhouettes. It has presented at Shanghai Fashion Week's New Bund 31 venue and returned for the Spring/Summer 2026 edition on October 13, 2025.

Cello Sonata is a womenswear designer label founded in London. Retail descriptions characterize its work as combining French-romantic and British influences with an emphasis on elegant clothing for urban women.

Belle Kids (百丽Kids) is the children's line of Belle (百丽), a leading Chinese footwear brand of Belle International. It extends the brand's “versatile, novel, classic and fashionable” product philosophy into children's shoes, bags, accessories and lifestyle products.
GUANJU (关雎记) appeared on the official Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026 schedule on October 14, 2025. No public brand biography, founder, or official website could be verified.
YIYI (译依) appeared on the official Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026 schedule on October 14, 2025. No public brand biography, founder, or official website could be verified.
ciciibear (齐齐熊/Qiqi Bear) is a Chinese childrenswear label sold through online marketplaces, known for new-Chinese-style pieces such as silk and tie-dye hanfu-inspired sets for boys and girls.

ili node is a Shanghai Fashion Week label founded by Li Jialun (李佳伦). The brand showed in the Spring/Summer 2026 edition, where season accessories coverage noted its collection among the participants.
See Also appeared on the official Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026 schedule on October 14, 2025. No public brand biography, founder, or official website could be verified.

DC KIDS is the childrenswear brand of Ningbo Jiuyao Garments Co., Ltd., founded by Ma Yunfa (马云发). The name derives from ‘direction’; the label is known for fresh, minimal styles in natural cotton and linen aimed at comfortable, healthy wear for children.

Jarelzhang is a Chinese designer label founded around 2016, known for a futuristic blend of streetwear and luxury with a post-apocalyptic aesthetic. Designer Jarel Zhang studied at Northumbria University and earned a master's in textile design from Chelsea College of Art and Design; collection credits list Chenxuan Zhang as creative director.

Husheguang Haute Couture is the couture label of Chinese-Dutch designer Hu Sheguang. His work is known for architectural silhouettes and for translating Chinese cultural references — including qipao, Yunjin brocade, ethnic motifs and Peking Opera — into contemporary couture.

Pantterfly is a Chinese label that showed in the Shanghai Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2026 edition; season accessories coverage noted its collection among the participants. No public brand biography, founder, or official website could be verified.
ONLY is a Danish womenswear brand founded in 1995 and owned by the BESTSELLER group. A high-street label with a denim focus, it entered the Chinese market in 1996.
丹▪DAN is the couture label of designer Zheng Xiaodan (郑小丹). Its refined womenswear pairs Eastern aesthetics with Western craft.

JS is the eponymous label of designer Jiangshuo (蒋硕), an associate professor at the Hebei Academy of Fine Arts and the founder and design director of the 肩上云 brand. Her couture work incorporates traditional Chinese cultural motifs to tell Chinese stories through clothing.

MARK FAIRWHALE (马克华菲) is a Chinese fashion brand founded in 2001 and led by designer Mark Cheung. Its “Born Trendy” positioning fuses contemporary cross-cultural and art references into commercial fashion.

RollingKids is a multi-brand children’s fashion and lifestyle retailer founded in China in 2017, curating global designer kidswear for ages 0–14 across apparel, footwear and accessories. It is operated by Rolling International (Shanghai) Trading Co., Ltd.

MARKGONG is the eponymous womenswear label of Chinese designer Mark Gong, launched in 2018 after his studies at Parsons and operating between New York and Shanghai. Built around the confident, independent “GONG GIRL”, its Spring/Summer 2026 collection “Catch Us If You Can” took loose inspiration from Thelma & Louise and was presented at Shanghai Fashion Week in collaboration with jewelry label YVMIN.
ABCKIDS is the core children’s footwear and apparel brand of Qibu Co., Ltd. (起步股份有限公司), covering shoes, clothing and accessories for children.

IKALI is a Chinese cultural-creative childrenswear brand built around game, anime and fairy-tale storytelling, including a “Five Princesses” concept developed by creative design director Amy. The brand is connected to Shanghai Yijialin Brand Development Co., Ltd.

YA YI is the eponymous label of designer Ya Yi, launched in New York in 2022 after her graduation from Parsons and roles at The Row, Thom Browne and AREA. Her work blends Eastern aesthetics with Western contexts to explore women’s and immigrant identities through textiles, craft, performance, film and installation; she was an LVMH Prize 2024 semifinalist.
FILA KIDS is the dedicated high-end children’s sports-fashion line of FILA, established as an independent kids’ brand in May 2015. FILA’s China business operates within ANTA Group.

shows.venue: The Atelier, Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai
shows.bio: Founded in 2012 by Amit Aggarwal, the eponymous label is known for sculptural couture and luxury prêt shaped through experimental materials such as polymers and liquid organza, combining futuristic structure with Indian handcraft; his March 28, 2025 show with Nothing featured futuristic designs in transparent and metallic materials.

The Mumbai couture label of husband-and-wife designers Falguni and Shane Peacock, known for dramatic embellished couture; their Lufthansa-partnered showcase closed Day 3 of the March 2025 edition on March 28.

New Delhi-based designer Namrata Joshipura’s eponymous label, known for contemporary womenswear; her March 28, 2025 show presented an athleisure collection developed with Reliance’s R|Elan fabric 2.0, with Malaika Arora and Kubra Sait as showstoppers.

Founded in 2008 by Rahul Mishra in New Delhi, known for handmade couture built on Indian handlooms, traditional craft, and intricate embroidery; his AFEW collection shown on March 29, 2025 was inspired by the natural world and the cycle of renewal.

The New Delhi luxury label of designers Shivan Bhatiya and Narresh Kukreja, known for high-end swimwear and resort wear; their March 29, 2025 show, presented in partnership with L’Atelier 1664, was staged as a living atelier from Paris to Mumbai.

The younger, edgier line S&N by brothers and designer duo Shantnu Mehra and Nikhil Mehra of Shantnu & Nikhil; their March 29, 2025 ‘Silver Starlight’ collection paired street glam with sharp tailoring, from rhinestone denim jackets to satin kurtas with metallic accents.

The House of Tarun Tahiliani, known for couture, bridal elegance and contemporary fashion blending Indian karigari with global finesse; his ‘OTT’ collection shown on March 29, 2025 delivered a bold modern bridal statement with Janhvi Kapoor as showstopper.

Launched in the UAE in 2004 by Landmark Group and introduced to India in 2006, a value-fashion retail brand known for affordable, trend-led clothing, footwear, and accessories for women, men, and children; it showcased on March 30, 2025.

shows.brand: FDCI x Pearl Academy: First Cut
shows.bio: ‘First Cut’ is the student showcase presented by Pearl Academy, India’s leading creative-education institution established in 1993, in collaboration with the FDCI, presenting the debut collections of final-year fashion students; the March 2025 edition took place on March 30.
shows.debut: Emerging student designer showcase

shows.venue: EENK Flagship Store, 3-4F, 43 Jangmun-ro, Yongsan-gu, Seoul
shows.bio: Created by designer Hyemee Lee, EENK is a Seoul label known for boldness and passion across fashion, art and lifestyle. Its signature Letter Project presents unique design items with alphabet-letter keywords from A to Z — collectibles, not disposables.

A Seoul-based boutique and made-to-order label led by sisters Sooy and Jay Park, JULYCOLUMN blends timeless craftsmanship with Korean traditional techniques, focusing on bespoke made-to-order garments made from sustainable, upcycled materials.

A denim brand launched in the United States in 2002 by a co-founder of True Religion, which moved its head office to Korea in 2017. Built on artisan-quality production, originality and sincere communication.

shows.venue: Jandi Sarangbang, 4F DDP Design Lab, Seoul
shows.bio: A Seoul-based high-end unisex label centered on womenswear, founded in 2020 by London College of Fashion graduate Bonbom Jo. Blending tailoring with streetwear and couture with real-way, the brand is known for its unique use of pleats and volume, and presents on the Paris Fashion Week calendar.

MMAM (Maison Modern Art Museum) is a contemporary designer brand founded by Hyun Park that adds doodle and graffiti drawing elements to modern classics, pursuing a near-minimalist silhouette mixed with maximalism.

A unisex contemporary label founded in 2021 by designer Kim Dae-sung upon his return to South Korea after studying at Istituto Marangoni in Milan and interning at Moschino. Its genderless, formal aesthetic combines bold color pairings with refined tailoring and a distinctly Korean design sensibility.

gaze de lin is a collection line by designer So Young Chang, started in 2012, with a soft avant-garde concept that proposes silhouettes maximizing women's beauty. Its GDeL line, launched in 2023, pursues sustainable fashion with 70% recycled materials and genderless, timeless, seasonless designs.

A Seoul-based boutique and made-to-order label led by sisters Sooy and Jay Park, JULYCOLUMN blends timeless craftsmanship with Korean traditional techniques, focusing on bespoke made-to-order garments made from sustainable, upcycled materials.

A denim brand launched in the United States in 2002 by a co-founder of True Religion, which moved its head office to Korea in 2017. Built on artisan-quality production, originality and sincere communication.

A Seoul-based high-end unisex label centered on womenswear, founded in 2020 by London College of Fashion graduate Bonbom Jo. Blending tailoring with streetwear and couture with real-way, the brand is known for its unique use of pleats and volume, and presents on the Paris Fashion Week calendar.

A ready-to-wear designer label from Seoul founded in 2012 by design duo Byungmun Seo and Jina Um. Originating in menswear with womenswear added in 2015, it is known for progressive construction, premium materials and a deconstructed take on classic luxury — 'weird but beautiful'.

Korean womenswear brand The Loom (더룸), trading as The Loom Atelier, officially listed in the WOMENS category of Seoul Fashion Week. Its Spring/Summer 2026 collection was presented at Seoul-ON, DDP, on September 5, 2025; visitor documentation of the presentation shows neutral-toned garments (whites, beiges, blacks), Hanbok-inspired silhouettes, and a standout red satin dress.

Founded in Seoul in 2021, GRACE ELWOOD explores the aesthetics of duality through deconstructed structures and sculptural silhouettes. Refined tailoring blends with playful, unconventional elements for a bold yet restrained mood.

A Seoul-based designer label from the Kumann studio founded in 1965, led by designer Hye Jin Yoo since 2010. Known for geometric, modern-art-inspired silhouettes with curved lines and asymmetric seam techniques.
A denim-based Seoul label led by designer Kwon Bong-seok; 'BLR' stands for 'Bluer Lives in the Rough', expressing a rough, opaque mood through the denim archive.

A Seoul-based designer brand founded in 2013 by directors Myungjun Shin and Hyunwoo Kim, redefining conventional standards with a blend of familiarity and novelty. Inspired by vintage beauty and diverse cultures, KIJUN creates a unique aesthetic that celebrates honesty, boldness and wit.
Fashion design studio founded by Nondumiso Mabunda in Dobsonville, Johannesburg, around 2020.
Streetwear label by Johannesburg designer Fulu Rathumbu; launched a limited-edition capsule with Monkey Shoulder at Soweto Fashion Week 2025.
Heritage luxury fashion and lifestyle brand founded in 2001, designing quintessential South African clothing and accessories; once dubbed 'Afro-Gucci' by Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung.
Label refining a tennis-style aesthetic with handcrafted embroidery, beadwork and hand-dyeing; its 'VALERIE' collection is named for the designer's late mother.
Streetwear brand of Designer Original Products Enterprise, founded 2009 by self-taught Johannesburg designer Andile Cele ('Scotchisdope'); inspired by basketball culture.

shows.venue: Blue Theatre, Soweto Theatre, Jabulani, Soweto
Blue Theatre, Soweto Theatre, Jabulani, Soweto
shows.bio: Streetwear brand of Designer Original Products Enterprise, founded 2009 by self-taught Johannesburg designer Andile Cele ('Scotchisdope'); inspired by basketball culture.

shows.venue: Blue Theatre, Soweto Theatre, Jabulani, Soweto
Blue Theatre, Soweto Theatre, Jabulani, Soweto
Blue Theatre, Soweto Theatre, Jabulani, Soweto
shows.bio: Fashion label of singer Wanda Baloyi, launched in 2023; debuted at Soweto Fashion Week with the 'Madelena' collection of coastal-chic, flowing feminine silhouettes, a tribute to her late grandmother and Mozambican heritage.

shows.venue: Blue Theatre, Soweto Theatre, Jabulani, Soweto
shows.bio: Diffusion ready-to-wear line launched by David Tlale at Soweto Fashion Week spring summer 25/26; price-conscious, relaxed everyday pieces with a comic-icon caricature of Tlale as its mascot; designed by his mentored creative team.

shows.venue: Blue Theatre, Soweto Theatre, Jabulani, Soweto
shows.bio: Fashion house based in Parow, Cape Town; showed at Soweto Fashion Week spring summer 25/26.

shows.venue: Blue Theatre, Soweto Theatre, Jabulani, Soweto
shows.bio: Fashion design studio founded by Nondumiso Mabunda in Dobsonville, Johannesburg, around 2020.

shows.venue: Spiral Garden and Spiral Café, Spiral, 5-6-23 Minami-Aoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo
shows.bio: Tokyo menswear label founded in 2016 by self-taught designer Kiichiro Asakawa (as stein; renamed ssstein for the Fall/Winter 2024 season). Known for quiet minimalism built on precision construction and exceptional Japan-made fabrics; winner of the FASHION PRIZE OF TOKYO 2025, which this event celebrated.

Meta Campania Collective is an artistic, quality-focused menswear label founded and led by creative director Jon Strassburg. Its Autumn/Winter 2026 collection, "Grisons," draws inspiration from Switzerland’s Grisons region.
Jeanne Friot is a Paris-based genderless label founded in 2020 by its namesake artistic director. The brand produces limited-edition pieces made from recycled and upcycled materials.
KML is a Saudi menswear label launched in 2022 by siblings Ahmed and Razan Hassan. It is the first Saudi ready-to-wear brand to appear on the official Paris fashion week calendar.
Études Studio is a Paris-based creative studio founded in 2012, working across menswear, book publishing, and artistic collaborations.
Valette Studio was founded in Paris in January 2020 by Pierre-François Valette. The label reinterprets the male wardrobe through atelier craft and traditional garment construction.
Founded in Tokyo in 2015 by Ryota Iwai; the label is known for luxurious Japanese fabrics and minimalist design.
Founded in Tokyo in 2014 by Hiroaki Sueyasu; the menswear label draws from punk and street culture.

shows.venue: DROPHAUS, Jardin d'Acclimatation, Bois de Boulogne
shows.bio: Founded in 1854 by Louis Vuitton as a Parisian trunk maker, long before it became a ready-to-wear house. Nicolas Ghesquière has led womenswear since 2013; Pharrell Williams leads menswear.

shows.venue: Kenzo Takada's former home, Bastille district
shows.bio: Founded in 1970 by Japanese designer Kenzo Takada; Nigo became artistic director in 2021. Part of LVMH.

Founded in 1996 in Stockholm by Jonny Johansson, part of a wider ACNE (“Ambition to Create Novel Expression”) creative collective spanning photography, art, and design. Johansson remains creative director.
3.Paradis was founded in 2013 by Emeric Tchatchoua. The label’s work centers on freedom, hope, and universalism.
The menswear line of Solid Homme, founded in Seoul in 1988; known for minimalist Korean menswear.
Founded in Paris in 1991 by Christophe Lemaire; the label, designed with Sarah-Linh Tran, is known for understated, functional elegance.

Founded in 1946 by Christian Dior; the 1947 “New Look” reshaped postwar fashion and still anchors the house's silhouette today. Jonathan Anderson became sole creative director in 2025, the first person to oversee womenswear, menswear, and couture together.
Founded in Paris in 1993 by Zio Song; the menswear house blends Eastern philosophy with Parisian tailoring.
Belgian designer, member of the Antwerp Six; his menswear is known for bold graphics and social commentary.
Founded in London in 2015 by Feng Chen Wang; the menswear label blends Chinese heritage with utilitarian design.
Egonlab is a Paris label founded in 2019 by Florentin Glémarec and Kévin Nompeix. It proposes gender-fluid tailoring that blends romantic and rebellious references.
Founded in Paris in 2011 by Alexandre Mattiussi; the menswear label offers relaxed Parisian chic with the Ami de Cœur logo.
Camperlab is the experimental sub-label of Spanish footwear company Camper, launched in 2015. Achilles Ion Gabriel became its creative director in 2019.
Ouest Paris is a menswear label founded by Arthur Robert in 2022. Its collections combine denim and workwear codes with references to Paris, Biarritz, and an imagined California.

The Miyake Design Studio was founded in Tokyo in 1970 by Issey Miyake, built on textile experimentation, pleating and technology. Satoshi Kondo has directed the ISSEY MIYAKE collection since Spring/Summer 2020.
shows.cd: Sen Kawahara, Yuki Itakura and Nobutaka Kobayashi

shows.bio: Founded in Los Angeles in 1994 by Rick Owens, the label is known for gothic, grunge-inflected architectural silhouettes. Owens' dark, monumental aesthetic has made him one of fashion's most distinctive independent voices.
Beijing-based menswear designer; the label is known for refined tailoring with Chinese cultural references.

New Delhi-based menswear label founded by Kartik Kumra, blending Indian artisan techniques — hand-spun, embroidered, naturally dyed fabrics — with streetwear; winner of the Fashion Trust Arabia 2025 Guest Country Award.

Established in 2020 by Sonia Martínez; tailoring, craftsmanship, and construction, revealing hidden garment-making processes. Martínez studied at IED Madrid and worked at Zara, Alexander McQueen, and Phoebe Philo's Céline.
Founded in Los Angeles in 2014 by Mike Amiri; the luxury menswear label blends rock-inspired aesthetics with Californian craftsmanship.

Founded by Yohji Yamamoto, who arrived in Paris from Tokyo in 1981 alongside Rei Kawakubo and upended Western ideas of tailoring with dark, fluid, deconstructed silhouettes. Still independently owned and designed by Yamamoto himself, a rarity in the industry.
The menswear line of System Homme, founded in Seoul; known for contemporary Korean menswear.
Founded in 1986 by Belgian designer Dries Van Noten, one of the original “Antwerp Six.” Julian Klausner became creative director in December 2024 after Van Noten’s own retirement.

Founded in 1992 by Junya Watanabe (b. 1961, Fukushima), a Rei Kawakubo protégé who trained as a Comme des Garçons patternmaker. Known as a pioneer of “techno-couture,” mixing advanced fabrics with inventive draping and construction.
Founded in Seoul in 2007 by Jung Wook Jun; the menswear label is known for oversized street-tailoring.
Lazoschmidl is a label founded in 2014 by Andreas Schmidl and Josef Lazo. Its work combines fashion, design, literature, and narrative storytelling.
Founded in Tokyo in 1996 by Mihara Yasuhiro; the label is known for the original sole sneaker and subversive design.
Founded in 2017 by Reid Baker and Ines Amorim; the menswear label reinterprets American classics.
New York-based menswear designer; the label explores Chicano culture and oversized tailoring.
The menswear line of Comme des Garçons, founded by Rei Kawakubo in Tokyo in 1969; Homme Plus presents avant-garde menswear in Paris.
Paris-based menswear designer; known for tailored menswear with a contemporary edge.
Founded in Los Angeles in 2018 by Eli Russell Linnetz; the label blends Californian youth culture with luxury.
Founded in Paris in 2012 by Pierre Mahéo; the menswear label offers timeless French wardrobe essentials.
Paris-based menswear designer; the label explores masculinity with surgical precision.
AMC is the label of Aldo Maria Camillo, founded in 2018. It focuses on tailoring and reinterpretations of classic male wardrobe archetypes.
Founded in 1993 by Jun Takahashi in Tokyo, rooted in the city's punk and subculture scene. Takahashi remains creative director of his own label.

Kiko Kostadinov is a London label founded by Bulgarian designer Kiko Kostadinov, known for workwear, uniforms and functional details. His experimental construction reworks utilitarian references into refined, forward-thinking design.
Founded in Tokyo in 2006 by Yosuke Aizawa; the outdoor-inspired label blends functionality with contemporary design.
C.R.E.O.L.E is the Paris label of designer Vincent Frédéric-Colombo. It proposes inclusive, gender-neutral fashion informed by Caribbean and diasporic culture and the idea of creolization.
Founded in Tokyo in 2004 by Junichi Abe; the menswear label is known for innovative pattern-making and color.

Maison Kitsuné is a Paris–Tokyo label founded in 2002, operating across fashion, music, and cafés. Abigail Smiley-Smith served as creative director for the Fall/Winter 2026 collection, the house’s first presentation on the official Paris calendar in seven years.
Founded in Bologna in 2016 by Luca Magliano; the menswear label explores Italian provincial identity with raw tailoring.
Shanghai-based menswear designer; the label is known for deconstructed tailoring with Chinese influences.
Launched in 2002 as a collaboration between Yohji Yamamoto and Adidas; the avant-garde sportswear line blends Japanese design with athletic function.
Founded in London in 2015 by Charles Jeffrey; the label is known for punk-inspired, club-kid menswear.
Founded in 2014 by Colm Dillane in New York, blending streetwear with theatrical, narrative-driven runway presentations.

French leather goods house founded in 1837 by Thierry Hermès. Nadège Vanhee-Cybulski has been artistic director of women’s ready-to-wear since 2014, prized for a decade-long tenure of stability in an industry defined by rotation.

Tokyo menswear label founded in 2016 by self-taught designer Kiichiro Asakawa (as stein; renamed ssstein for the Fall/Winter 2024 season). Known for quiet minimalism built on precision construction and exceptional Japan-made fabrics; winner of the FASHION PRIZE OF TOKYO 2025, which this event celebrated.
Founded in 1999 by Chitose Abe in Tokyo, known for “splicing” two or more garments into one hybrid piece. Abe remains creative director of her own label.
Founded in Paris in 2002 by Youngmi Woo; the South Korean menswear label is known for architectural tailoring.
Founded in Tokyo in 2012 by Masayuki Ino; the menswear label won the 2018 LVMH Prize, known for playful subversion.
Founded in Seoul in 2018; the technical menswear label is known for deconstructed utilitarian design.
Amsterdam-based menswear designer; the label is known for oversized, deconstructed tailoring.
Founded in Tokyo in 2013 by Takuya Morikawa; the menswear label is known for experimental textiles.
Founded in Paris in 1975 by Agnès Troublé, agnès b. is known for simple, timeless clothing — including the iconic snap cardigan. The brand's understated French style has endured as a wardrobe staple.
Founded in Tokyo in 2010 by Shinpei Yamagishi; the menswear label reimagines American classics with Japanese precision.
Founded in 1965 in Paris by Léon-Claude Duhamel, who created the original foldable nylon rain jacket. The brand celebrated its 60th anniversary in 2025.
Founded in 1978 in Solomeo, Italy, by Brunello Cucinelli; the luxury house is known for cashmere and understated Italian elegance.
Founded in 1986 by Dirk Bikkembergs; the Belgian-Italian sportswear brand blends fashion and football culture.
Founded in 1974 in Brescia, Italy; the menswear brand is known for deconstructed tailoring and the K-Jacket.
Founded in 1910 in Trivero, Italy, by Ermenegildo Zegna as a wool mill; the family-owned luxury menswear house is known for fine fabrics and modern tailoring.
Eponymous Italian leather and outerwear label designed by Salvatore Santoro.
Founded in 1967 by Ralph Lauren, built on an aspirational, preppy vision of American style — the polo player logo among the most recognized in fashion.
Milan-rooted collaborative fashion project launched in 2021 by Nathalie Danten.
Milan-born upcycling and sportswear designer; founder of his eponymous label.
Italian premium denim label presented as a digital release at Milan Fashion Week for Fall/Winter 2025.
Founded in 1995 by Canadian twin designers Dean and Dan Caten. The Fall/Winter 2025 co-ed runway show celebrated the brand's 30th anniversary.
Founded in 1968 in Naples by Ciro Paone; the luxury menswear house is renowned for Neapolitan tailoring and handcrafted garments.
Founded in 1978 in Filottrano, Italy, by the Lardini brothers; the menswear brand is known for modern tailoring with artisanal details.
Founded in 1873 in Northampton, England; the luxury footwear maker is known for Goodyear-welted shoes, part of Prada Group since 1999.
Founded in Rome in 1945 by Nazareno Fonticoli and Gaetano Savini; the Italian menswear house is renowned for sartorial ready-to-wear and bespoke tailoring, acquired by Kering in 2011.
Technical outerwear label founded by Alessandro Pungetti and Paul Harvey.
Label founded by Satoshi Kuwata, fusing Japanese and Western craftsmanship; winner of the 2023 LVMH Prize.
Genderless luxury label founded by Giulio Maragno in spring 2021, working with upcycled deadstock fabrics.

Founded in 1985 in Legnano by Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana, epitomizing Italian glamour and sensuality. Gabbana stepped down as chairman in late 2025 but remains co-creative director alongside Dolce.

Founded in 1851 in Switzerland by Carl Franz Bally, the label has long been known for leather craftsmanship and shoes; Simone Bellotti was creative director for Fall/Winter 2025 before moving to Jil Sander.
Italian menswear house in the quiet-luxury vein.
Menswear label founded by designer Ludovico Bruno.
Founded in 1970 in Quinto Vicentino, Italy; the menswear brand is part of the Forall group, known for refined Italian tailoring.
Founded in Naples in 1986; the Italian brand is known for the dachshund logo and preppy Mediterranean style.
Label founded in 2016 by Yushan Li and Jun Zhou.
Founded in 1930 in Mantua, Italy; the menswear house is known for sartorial tailoring and Made in Italy quality.
Milan upcycling project founded in 2020, reworking home textiles into garments.
Paul Smith is the British fashion house founded by designer Paul Smith. The label's March 19, 2025 presentation was its Tokyo runway debut, staged under the ‘by R’ banner.
Founded in 1982 in Italy by Massimo Osti; the sportswear brand is renowned for innovative fabric treatments and the compass badge.
Caribbean-rooted label founded by creative director Geoff K. Cooper.
Menswear project by Naples-raised brothers Gianmarco and Francesco Marano.

Founded in Milan by Simone Cracker (b. 1985), who began in 2006 making accessories from upholstery materials before officially launching Simon Cracker in 2010. Built entirely on giving old and unused clothes and materials new life through patchwork and upcycling.
Founded in Milan in 2007 by Marco Baldassari and Paolo Zuntini; the menswear brand is known for smart-casual luxury with Made in Italy craftsmanship.
Label founded by Khalid Al Qasimi; Hoor Al Qasimi is creative director.

Founded in 2022 by Ghanaian-born designer Victor Reginald Bob Abbey-Hart in Milan, known for architectural denim tailoring fusing military and workwear influences with Made-in-Italy craftsmanship. Debuted at Milan Fashion Week Men's in 2026 with the 'Anatomy of Void' collection.
Milanese label founded in 2017, presented as a digital release at Milan Fashion Week for Fall/Winter 2025.

Founded in 1913 by Mario Prada in Milan as a leather goods shop; became a fashion house under Miuccia Prada from the 1980s on. Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons have served as co-creative directors since 2020.
Menswear house founded in 1965 by Michele Latorre.
Label founded in 2018 by London designer and choreographer Saul Nash.
Founded in 1934 in Triuggio, Italy, by Giacomo Canali; the family-owned menswear house is known for sartorial tailoring and Made in Italy craftsmanship.
Eponymous label launched in 2013 by designer Brett Johnson.
Menswear label founded in 2018 by Matteo Lamandini.
Menswear project founded in 2022.

Roots trace to a shoemaking workshop founded by Filippo Della Valle in the early 1900s in the Marche region; his grandson Diego Della Valle built it into the global Tod’s brand, best known for the hand-stitched, rubber-studded Gommino driving shoe.

Founded in 1927 by Salvatore Ferragamo, the shoemaker to Hollywood’s golden age. Maximilian Davis has been creative director since 2022, bringing a contemporary, playful edge while staying rooted in the house’s codes.
Founded by Gimmo Etro, known for its signature paisley print. A family business: children Kean, Veronica, and Jacopo Etro have led menswear, womenswear, and accessories respectively.
Label founded in 2016 by Francesco Rossini.
Menswear house founded in 2006 by Fabio Peroni.
Namesake experimental menswear brand founded in 2022 by Domenico Orefice; January 2026 was its official CNMI-calendar Milan debut.
Sustainable genderless tailoring label founded in Tuscany in 2021 by Annachiara Bernardi.
Namesake menswear label founded in 2013 by Spanish designer David Catalán, working between Porto and Madrid.

Founded in 1988 by Portuguese designer Miguel Vieira, known for refined tailoring and luxurious eveningwear in silk and satin with a sophisticated, modern sensibility. A longtime fixture of Portugal Fashion, he has shown internationally from São Paulo to Milan.

Founded in 1975 by Giorgio Armani, who redefined masculine and feminine elegance through deconstructed, minimalist tailoring. Armani passed away in September 2025 at age 91; his niece Silvana Armani, already his longtime design deputy, now leads ready-to-wear.

Founded in 1975 by Giorgio Armani, who redefined masculine and feminine elegance through deconstructed, minimalist tailoring. Armani passed away in September 2025 at age 91; his niece Silvana Armani, already his longtime design deputy, now leads ready-to-wear.
Founded in 1975 in California by Jim Jannard; the eyewear and apparel brand is known for performance innovation, owned by Luxottica.
Recycled and deadstock knitwear collective, with Shun Giovanni Colafato and Michele Nigra in creative and artistic direction.
Label founded in Milan in 2024 by Filippo Cascinelli Staudacher.
Ivorian menswear label founded in 2017 by Aristide Loua.
South Korean label designed by Halyn Kim and Young Dae Kong.
Ghanaian sustainable unisex concept founded in 2018 by Christopher Akpo.
Ghanaian unisex label founded in 2018 by Travis Obeng-Casper.
ANCELLM is the men's ready-to-wear and accessories label of designer Kazuya Yamachika, exploring aging, changing tones and textures.

Tokyo-based label launched in 2004 by Yoshio Kubo, who graduated from Philadelphia University's Textile & Science school in 2000, assisted Robert Danes in New York for four years, and returned to Japan in 2004.

TANAKA is the Tokyo-based menswear label of designer Kuboshita, built around cyanotype printing and Japanese denim and leather chosen to age with the wearer; its Fall/Winter 2026 collection was themed “Blue Print”.

Parisian couture house founded by Elsa Schiaparelli, famed for surrealist couture and legendary collaborations with artists including Dalí, Cocteau, Man Ray, and Giacometti; Daniel Roseberry is creative director.

shows.venue: Private residence of perfumer Daniela Andrier
shows.bio: Parisian made-to-order label by designer Julie de Libran, producing in limited quantities from end-of-roll and deadstock fabrics.
Lebanese couture house founded by Georges Hobeika, artistically directed by Georges and Jad Hobeika and known for hand-embroidered couture eveningwear.

shows.debut: Jonathan Anderson's first Dior couture collection — and his first couture outing.
shows.bio: Parisian house founded by Christian Dior in 1946, synonymous with the New Look; Jonathan Anderson is creative director.
Indian couture house led by designer Rahul Mishra, known for meticulously hand-embroidered couture honoring Indian craft communities.
Cameroonian-born former dancer and model whose Paris couture house joins African textile traditions with Parisian couture.

shows.debut: Matthieu Blazy's haute couture debut for Chanel.
shows.bio: Parisian couture house founded by Gabrielle 'Coco' Chanel; Matthieu Blazy is creative director.
Indian couture label founded by Gaurav Gupta in 2004, known for sculptural, futuristic couture.
Parisian haute couture house led by designer Stéphane Rolland, presenting sculptural couture during Paris Haute Couture Week.
Parisian couture house founded by Julien Fournié in 2009, holding the official Haute Couture appellation since 2017.
Couture label by Dutch designer Ronald van der Kemp, crafting couture from surplus, vintage, reclaimed, and repurposed materials.

shows.debut: First Privé show after Giorgio Armani's death in September 2025; Silvana Armani's debut leading Privé.
shows.bio: The haute couture line of the Italian house founded by Giorgio Armani in 1975; led by Silvana Armani since Giorgio Armani's death in September 2025.
Parisian couture house led by designer Alexis Mabille, known for elegant, precise couture.
Parisian haute couture house led by Franck Sorbier, holding the official haute couture appellation since 2005.
Lebanese couture house founded by Elie Saab, celebrated for opulent hand-embroidered couture and red-carpet gowns.
Couture house led by Japanese designer Yuima Nakazato, a Royal Academy of Fine Arts Antwerp graduate, fusing traditional craftsmanship with innovative techniques.
Italian couture house founded in Rome by Valentino Garavani; the January 2026 couture was designed by creative director Alessandro Michele, shown shortly after Garavani's death.
Amsterdam-based avant-garde couture house founded in 1993 by Dutch designers Viktor Horsting and Rolf Snoeren, known for conceptual, sculptural couture.
Lebanese couture house founded by Zuhair Murad, known for lavishly embroidered couture and red-carpet gowns.
Couture house founded in 2014 by Hong Kong-born, London-based designer Robert Wun, known for conceptual, sculptural, trompe-l'oeil couture.
Couture house founded by Sofia Crociani in 2017, describing itself as ecological, ethical, cruelty-free art-to-wear couture made from natural, organic, vintage, or reused materials.
Paris-based couture house by Dutch designer Peet Dullaert, who founded his label in 2012; his couture emphasizes movement, structure, and handcraft.
Couture house led by Saudi-born designer Mohammed Ashi, known for architectural silhouettes and couture craftsmanship.

shows.debut: The house's official Paris Haute Couture Week debut — the first Vietnam-based designer on the official schedule — with 'Cành Vàng Lá Ngọc – The Golden Branch and Jade Leaf'.
shows.bio: Couture maison founded in 2023 by creative director Phan Huy with Steven Doan, combining Vietnamese craft traditions with sculptural contemporary couture.
Greek couture house with a legacy dating to 1906 in Athens, led by couturier Celia Kritharioti and known for opulent handwork, embroidery, and eveningwear.
Syrian-born, Dubai-based couturier Rami Al Ali, whose work combines architectural draping with Middle Eastern craft references.

London-based couture house founded in 2020 by South Korean designer Sohee Park, drawing on Korean heritage and intricate couture craft; Park is a Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree and Business of Fashion 500 member.
Couture house led by Swiss designer Kévin Germanier, known for couture crafted from upcycled and discarded materials.

Parisian couture house founded by Elsa Schiaparelli, famed for surrealist couture and legendary collaborations with artists including Dalí, Cocteau, Man Ray, and Giacometti; Daniel Roseberry is creative director.
Cameroonian-born former dancer and model whose Paris couture house joins African textile traditions with Parisian couture.
Couture house founded by Iris van Herpen in 2007, combining traditional craftsmanship with technology, science, architecture, and art.
Lebanese couture house founded by Georges Hobeika, artistically directed by Georges and Jad Hobeika and known for hand-embroidered couture eveningwear.
Parisian house founded by Christian Dior in 1946, synonymous with the New Look; Jonathan Anderson is creative director.

Chanel presented its Cruise 2026 collection at Villa d'Este on Lake Como on April 29, 2025, created by the house's Creation Studio between Virginie Viard's departure and Matthieu Blazy's debut that September. Silk headscarves made in Como, a white tweed coat nodding to a hotel robe, and gelato-tub handbags channeled off-duty Riviera glamour.

Gucci staged its Cruise 2026 show, titled 'Gucci Is Florence, Florence Is Gucci,' at Palazzo Settimanni — the house's archive — in Florence on May 15, 2025, designed by the in-house team between Sabato De Sarno's exit and Demna's arrival. The collection doubled down on house codes with amped-up Italian glamour, closing as models walked out of the palazzo into the Florentine evening.

shows.venue: Cour d'Honneur, Palais des Papes, Avignon
shows.bio: Nicolas Ghesquière presented Louis Vuitton's Cruise 2026 collection in the Cour d'Honneur of the Palais des Papes in Avignon on May 22, 2025, with a theatrical set by Es Devlin. The collection fused medieval references — rich brocades, leg-of-mutton sleeves, ruffles — with the designer's coolly futuristic hand.

Maria Grazia Chiuri presented her final Dior collection, Cruise 2026, in the gardens of Rome's Villa Albani Torlonia on May 27, 2025 — a homecoming to the city where she was born and raised. The 'Bella Confusione'-themed show drew on Renaissance gowns, mid-century Cinecittà glamour, and ecclesiastical vestments.

Ian Griffiths closed the Cruise 2026 season with Max Mara's Resort 2026 collection, 'Venere Vesuviana,' at the Reggia di Caserta outside Naples on June 17, 2025. Inspired by the dress codes of 1950s Neapolitan women and icons like Sophia Loren, the show paired voluptuous tailoring with flat tasseled loafers.

Sara Cavazza Facchini presented Genny's Cruise 2026 collection at Casa Lago in the Hollywood Hills, Los Angeles, on June 1, 2025, during an event celebrating Italy's Republic Day organized by the Italian Consulate General. The house's signature orchid print reappeared in lime tones across fluid evening gowns, jeweled denim, and relaxed tailoring.

Founded in Paris in 2009 by Simon Porte Jacquemus; the French label is known for playful, sun-drenched designs and viral runway moments. Its Fall/Winter 2026 “Le Palmier” collection closed Paris Men’s Fashion Week on January 25, 2026 at the Musée Picasso — officially a menswear-week show presented as a co-ed runway, with both menswear and womenswear looks.
